## Numbers and symbols

- **3-2-1-1-0 rule** — Backup guideline of three copies, two media, one off-site, one immutable or offline, and zero restore-verification errors. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))

## A

- **Accelerator utilisation (AU)** — the share of time a simulated accelerator spends computing rather than waiting for data; MLPerf Storage results must stay above a threshold. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **Acknowledgement point** — the moment a storage system tells the host that a write is durable. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Active recall** — Producing an answer from memory before checking it, rather than rereading the material. ([Ch 59](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/59-self-test-flashcards.md))
- **Active/non-optimized path** — A working path that costs an extra internal hop and is used only when optimized paths fail. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Active/optimized path** — A path the array advertises as the preferred, lowest-latency route to a volume. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Active/passive** — A controller arrangement in which one controller serves all I/O while the other waits to take over. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Adam optimizer** — The standard optimizer for large models, which stores a running mean (first moment) and running variance (second moment) of each parameter's gradient. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **AFR (annualized failure rate)** — The fraction of devices expected to fail per year of operation. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **AFX** — NetApp's disaggregated all-flash ONTAP system in which controllers share NVMe enclosures over a fabric. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Agent rollback** — Undoing changes an AI agent made to files, databases or configurations, typically by restoring from snapshots or backups. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Agentic AI** — AI systems that plan and carry out multi-step tasks by calling tools and data sources, not just answering a single prompt. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Agentic operations** — Infrastructure management in which AI agents diagnose and, within limits, act on systems rather than only advise. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **AGPLv3** — A copyleft open-source licence that requires sharing source code even when software is offered over a network. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **AHV** — Nutanix's hypervisor, the main destination for many VMware migrations. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **AI agent** — An LLM-driven program that plans and executes multi-step tasks by calling tools, APIs and data sources. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **AI Data Engine (AIDE)** — NetApp's ONTAP extension that indexes, vectorises and governs data for AI pipelines. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **AI data pipeline** — The end-to-end flow of data through ingest, curation, training, checkpointing, fine-tuning, inference, RAG and agents, each with its own storage I/O pattern. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **AI factory** — NVIDIA's term for a data centre whose GPUs, networks, storage and software are designed as one production line whose output is AI tokens. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **AI infrastructure tracker (IDC)** — IDC's quarterly measure of server and storage spending deployed for AI workloads. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **AI momentum** — The atlas's composite of 2025–26 evidence of AI-driven growth: revenue, bookings, valuation, design wins, benchmarks and shipping AI features. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **AI-native depth** — How much of the AI data path a vendor serves on architecture it owns and designed for AI workloads. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **AI-native storage vendor** — A storage company whose growth and roadmap centre on GPU-cluster workloads, such as VAST Data, WEKA and DDN. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **AI-Q blueprint** — NVIDIA's reference agent workflow that uses NeMo Retriever microservices to search enterprise data. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **AI400X series** — DDN's 2U all-NVMe EXAScaler appliances (AI400X, AI400X2, AI400X3, AI400X3M), each generation raising bandwidth per box. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **AIOps** — Use of analytics and machine learning on infrastructure telemetry to predict faults, open tickets and recommend or take corrective actions. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **AIStor** — MinIO's commercial object storage product, sold as Free and Enterprise editions after the community edition was archived. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **All Software Included** — Pure Storage's original licensing model in which every Purity software feature came with the array at no extra charge. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **Alletra Storage MP** — HPE's common storage hardware platform that runs B10000 block and X10000 object/file software. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Alletra Storage MP X10000** — HPE's disaggregated object store with native NFS, aimed at AI data and KV-cache offload. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **ALUA (Asymmetric Logical Unit Access)** — The SCSI standard by which an array tells hosts which paths to a volume are optimized, non-optimized, standby or unavailable. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **ANA (Asymmetric Namespace Access)** — NVMe's multipathing mechanism that reports which paths to a namespace are optimized, the counterpart of SCSI ALUA. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **ANN (approximate nearest neighbour) search** — Similarity search that trades a small loss of recall for orders-of-magnitude speed-ups over scanning every vector. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Antitrust remedy** — A divestiture or behavioural commitment that regulators require before clearing a deal. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Anvil** — Hammerspace's metadata server that holds the global namespace and hands out pNFS layouts. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Apache Iceberg** — An open table format that adds snapshots, atomic commits, schema evolution and time travel to collections of files in object storage. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Apache Parquet** — An open columnar file format optimised for analytic scans, storing columns in compressed pages inside large row groups. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Approved vendor list (AVL)** — A platform owner's list of qualified component suppliers that reference designs may use. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **Approved-vendor list** — Board-language shorthand for NVIDIA's storage certifications, which gate entry to most GPU-cluster deals without ranking vendors. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Architectural maximum** — the largest configuration a design allows in principle, before testing and support limits. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Architectural pendulum** — The recurring swing of storage design between centralized pools, distributed nodes and disaggregated fabrics as media, network and CPU costs change. ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Architecture decision matrix** — A grid rating each storage architecture against each workload, used to pick a starting design before comparing vendors. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **Architecture review** — a structured walk through a system's data path, metadata, failure domains, upgrades, scale limits, performance claims and roadmap dependencies. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Archive storage** — The tier that retains rarely accessed data for years at the lowest cost per terabyte, often on tape or cloud archive classes. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Areal density** — Bits stored per unit area of a disk platter or chip, the main driver of cost per bit. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **ARR multiple** — A purchase price or valuation divided by the target's annual recurring revenue. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Array controller software** — The operating environment of a storage system (e.g., Purity, ONTAP) that runs placement, RAID or erasure coding, snapshots, replication and data reduction. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **ASC 606** — The US GAAP revenue-recognition standard that times revenue to the transfer of control of goods or the delivery of services. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **ASC 842** — The US GAAP lease standard that puts most leases on the lessee's balance sheet and defines when a contract contains a lease. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **Asymmetric active/active** — A controller arrangement in which each controller owns some volumes and forwards I/O for volumes it does not own. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Asynchronous checkpointing** — Saving training state by copying it quickly to host memory and writing it to storage in the background while training continues. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md), [Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Asynchronous replication** — Replication that acknowledges locally and ships changes later, so recent writes can be lost. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Atlas judgment** — a label for the atlas's own synthesis of public facts, such as quadrant placements or threat rankings. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Attach rate** — The share of an installed customer base that buys an additional product. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md), [Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **Augmented Memory Grid** — WEKA's NeuralMesh feature that streams KV cache between GPU memory and shared flash over RDMA and GPUDirect Storage. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **Augmented Memory Grid (AMG)** — WEKA's KV-cache offload tier that stores evicted attention key/value blocks on pooled NVMe and streams them back to GPUs. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md), [Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Azure Managed Lustre** — Microsoft Azure's managed Lustre parallel file system service. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Azure Native Qumulo** — Qumulo's scale-out file service sold and billed inside Microsoft Azure. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **A³I (Accelerated, Any-scale AI)** — DDN's family of EXAScaler appliances and reference designs sized for NVIDIA GPU clusters. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))

## B

- **Back-end compute fabric** — The InfiniBand or Ethernet network that carries GPU-to-GPU traffic between racks in an AI cluster, kept separate from storage and front-end traffic. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **Back-end fabric** — The network that connects storage compute nodes to storage media, separate from the front-end network clients use. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Back-invalidate** — A CXL 3.0 mechanism that lets a memory device recall cache lines from hosts, enabling coherent multi-host sharing. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Bandwidth per TB** — The throughput a device or system can deliver per terabyte stored, which falls as hard drives grow larger. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Baseline question** — A follow-up that asks what a performance or savings claim is measured against. ([Ch 57](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/57-question-bank.md))
- **BeeGFS** — A parallel file system developed by ThinkParQ, a 2014 Fraunhofer spin-off, with separate management, metadata and storage services. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Benchmark normalisation** — dividing a benchmark result by rack units, power, price or capacity so that differently sized systems can be compared. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md), [Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **BiCS** — Toshiba/Kioxia's 3D NAND architecture, announced in 2007 and now built jointly with Sandisk. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Binding constraint** — The single requirement in a deal that eliminates most options before price or performance is compared. ([Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Bit growth** — The year-on-year increase in total NAND (or DRAM) bits supplied or demanded, the key supply-demand variable in memory markets. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Bit share** — a supplier's share of total NAND capacity shipped, as opposed to its share of revenue. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Bits per cell** — The number of bits stored in one flash cell (SLC 1, MLC 2, TLC 3, QLC 4, PLC 5), set by how many voltage states the cell must distinguish. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Blast radius** — How much data or service a single component failure can take offline or put into rebuild. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md), [Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Blended gross margin** — A company's overall gross margin as the revenue-weighted mix of higher-margin software and lower-margin hardware. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Block protocol** — A protocol that lets a host read and write numbered fixed-size blocks on a remote device, with no notion of files. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Block storage** — Storage presented as a volume of numbered fixed-size blocks whose meaning is managed by the host's file system or database. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Bloom filter** — A compact probabilistic structure that answers "definitely not present" cheaply, used to avoid deduplication index lookups for new data. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **BlueField-4 STX** — NVIDIA's 2026 modular storage reference architecture in which storage services run on BlueField-4 DPUs. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md), [Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md), [Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Board language** — Storage jargon restated in terms of cost, risk, speed or revenue quality for a CFO or board audience. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Bounce buffer** — A staging area in host (CPU) memory that data passes through on its way between storage or the network and GPU memory. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Bucket** — The container in an object store that holds objects and carries policy, region, billing and versioning settings. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md), [Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Bucket index sharding** — Splitting one bucket's key index into multiple shards so that writes and LIST requests spread across servers. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Buffer-to-buffer credits** — Fibre Channel's flow-control scheme, in which a sender transmits only as many frames as the receiver has buffers for, so frames are never dropped for congestion. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Build / buy / partner** — The three ways a company can obtain a capability: develop it in-house, acquire it, or contract for it with another firm. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Build, partner or defer** — the three answers a PM can give to a product gap. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **Bulk-data hop** — One network traversal that a data byte makes between the flash that stores it and the client that reads or writes it. ([Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Bundled scaling** — The constraint that each added node brings a fixed ratio of compute, cache, capacity and network ports. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Busy polling** — Having a dedicated CPU core repeatedly check for completed I/O instead of waiting for an interrupt, trading CPU for lower, steadier latency. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Byte-range GET** — An S3 read of only a specified byte range of an object, used to parallelise large reads. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Bε-tree (B-epsilon tree)** — A write-optimised B-tree whose internal nodes buffer pending updates and push them down in batches, turning small random writes into large sequential ones. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))

## C

- **Cached disk array** — A storage array that fronts many commodity disks with a large RAM cache so most I/O never waits for a disk (EMC Symmetrix, 1990). ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **CAP theorem** — The result that during a network partition a distributed system must give up either consistency or availability. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Capability heatmap** — A vendor-by-capability table using filled, half-filled and empty marks to show how fully each vendor offers each capability. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Capacity buffer** — Spare capacity a storage-as-a-service vendor guarantees to keep installed above the customer's current use (25% for Evergreen//One). ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Capex discipline** — a memory maker's restraint in adding wafer capacity, used to keep supply tight and prices firm. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Capex purchase** — Buying storage outright as a capital asset that the customer owns, depreciates and eventually replaces. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **Capsule** — An NVMe-oF message carrying a command or a response, and optionally in-line data. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Catch-up launch** — An incumbent product built to close an architectural gap that challengers opened first. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Causal consistency** — A guarantee that no reader sees a write without also seeing the earlier writes it depends on. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **CBox** — VAST's server chassis containing multiple CNodes. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Ceph RGW** — The RADOS Gateway, Ceph's S3-compatible object interface. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **CephFS** — Ceph's POSIX file system interface. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Ceres** — VAST's 2022 storage-enclosure (DBox) design that uses NVIDIA BlueField DPUs as its fabric endpoints. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Chain replication** — A replication scheme in which writes flow along an ordered chain of servers (primary to replica) and are acknowledged once the chain has persisted them. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Charge-trap cell** — The 3D NAND cell design that stores electrons in a silicon-nitride layer around a vertical channel instead of in a floating gate. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Checkpoint** — A periodic snapshot of model weights and optimizer state written during training so a job can restart after a failure. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md), [Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Checkpoint drain** — The background transfer of a checkpoint from host memory or local NVMe to durable shared storage. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Chunk (object store)** — A large fixed-size container (128 MB in Dell ObjectScale) into which many objects are packed before erasure coding. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Chunk Store** — Tectonic's flat storage layer that holds data chunks on storage nodes. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Chunking** — Splitting documents into small passages (typically a few hundred tokens) before embedding them for retrieval. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Clean team** — A ring-fenced group allowed to review competitively sensitive material, such as source code, during a deal. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Client eviction** — A server's forced removal of an unresponsive client's locks and state, which can lose that client's cached writes. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Client-side NFS multipath** — A modified NFS client (for example VAST's) that spreads one mount across many local NICs and many server addresses. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **Clone** — A writable snapshot that shares unchanged blocks with its source. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Close-to-open consistency** — The NFS guarantee that one client's writes become visible to another client only after the writer closes the file and the reader reopens it. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **Closed division** — the MLPerf category with fixed benchmark code and few tunables, intended for like-for-like comparison. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **Cloud block storage** — Hyperscaler-run network block volumes, such as AWS EBS, attached to cloud instances. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md), [Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **Cluster map** — The authoritative record of a cluster's membership, health and placement rules, versioned by epoch. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **ClusterMAX** — SemiAnalysis's rating system for GPU clouds, scoring providers on ten criteria including storage. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **CMR / ePMR** — Conventional (non-overlapping) perpendicular magnetic recording, including energy-assisted variants, the mainstream HDD technology before HAMR. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **CMX** — NVIDIA's rack-scale context-memory storage platform for KV cache, the first implementation of STX. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md), [Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md), [Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md), [Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **CMX (context memory storage)** — NVIDIA's BlueField-4-based, Ethernet-attached flash tier for KV cache at pod level, labelled "G3.5". ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **CNode** — VAST's stateless compute node that runs protocols, data reduction and erasure coding but holds no authoritative state. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **CNode-X** — A VAST compute node with NVIDIA GPUs, announced in February 2026, for GPU-accelerated vector search and SQL inside the storage cluster. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Co-packaged optics (CPO)** — Optical engines packaged next to a switch or processor die instead of in pluggable modules, cutting power and laser count. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Colossus** — Google's cluster-level distributed file system and the successor to GFS, underpinning Cloud Storage, YouTube and Gmail. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Command set vs. transport** — The split between what a storage protocol says (SCSI or NVMe commands) and how it travels (PCIe, FC, RDMA or TCP). ([Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **Committed ARR** — A private company's own measure of contracted annual recurring revenue (used by VAST); not an audited figure. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Committed ARR (CARR)** — The annualised value of signed recurring contracts, including those not yet live, so it runs ahead of ARR. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md), [Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Commoditisation risk** — The danger that a software layer above the arrays (for example a global namespace) makes storage hardware interchangeable. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Community fork** — An independently maintained copy of an open-source project created when the original owner stops maintaining or restricts it. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Compaction** — Background rewriting of many small data files into fewer large ones to keep table queries fast. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Company-stated** — a label for a private company's own unaudited figure. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Competitive matrix** — A chart or grid placing vendors on chosen dimensions so their relative positions can be compared at a glance. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Computational storage** — Placing processing in or beside a storage device to operate on data before it crosses the host interface. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Conditional write** — A PUT that succeeds only if a precondition holds (the key is absent or its ETag matches), giving optimistic concurrency control. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Configuration master** — A separate service that records which servers form each replication chain and changes membership after failures. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Confused deputy** — A security flaw in which a privileged service is tricked into using its authority for a caller who lacks it. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Consensus** — A protocol by which a group of machines agrees on one ordered log of operations despite crashes and lost messages. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Consistency model** — The contract that defines which version of data a reader may see when copies of it disagree. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Consistent hashing** — A placement scheme that maps keys and nodes onto a ring so that adding or removing a node moves only about 1/N of the data. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Content-aware storage** — IBM's Storage Scale capability that embeds and indexes data inside the file system for retrieval-augmented AI. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Content-defined chunking (CDC)** — Cutting data where a rolling hash over the content matches a pattern, so chunk boundaries survive insertions. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Content-derived metadata** — Metadata produced by reading and classifying the content itself, such as "contains PII" or "EU customer record". ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Context memory** — A storage tier that holds inference KV cache between GPU memory and shared storage so that long conversations need not be recomputed. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Contract price** — the negotiated quarterly or monthly price that large buyers pay NAND or DRAM makers, as distinct from the more volatile spot price. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md), [Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Control plane** — The part of a storage system that holds desired state (volumes, policies, placement) and configures the data plane, operating in seconds rather than microseconds. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Control point** — the layer of the stack that owns the customer relationship and the metadata, and so captures most of the value. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md))
- **Controller VM (CVM)** — Nutanix's per-node virtual machine that runs the storage service in an HCI cluster. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Converged mode** — A deployment in which storage software runs on the same servers as the applications or GPUs, using their local drives. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Conversation playbook** — the section of every chapter with questions for PMs and engineers, strong-answer sketches and misconceptions to avoid. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Coordinator node** — The cluster node a client connects to, which computes data placement and fans reads and writes out to peer nodes. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Copy-on-write (COW) snapshot** — Snapshot method that copies an old block to a reserve area before overwriting it in place. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Copyleft** — Licence terms, as in GPL and AGPL, that require derived works to be distributed under the same terms with source available. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Copyset** — A fixed group of nodes that together hold all replicas of some chunks; limiting copysets makes data loss events rarer. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Correlated failure** — Multiple failures with a shared cause (batch, firmware, power, software upgrade) that strike together and break independence assumptions. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md), [Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Credibility ladder** — the progression from L1 to L3 knowledge that sets how far an expert will engage with you. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md), [Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **CRUSH** — Ceph's placement algorithm, which computes the drives for each placement group from a hierarchical cluster map and failure-domain rules, without a lookup table. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)** — The standard plug-in interface through which Kubernetes asks a storage system to create, attach and delete volumes. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **cuFile** — The programming interface for GPUDirect Storage that applications call instead of POSIX read and write to move file data into or out of GPU memory. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Cumulative bookings** — The total value of all contracts a company has ever signed, including multi-year commitments not yet recognised as revenue. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **cuObject** — NVIDIA's client and server libraries implementing RDMA for S3-compatible object storage. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md), [Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Curator** — A Colossus metadata server; curators store file-system metadata in Bigtable and scale horizontally. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Custodian** — A Colossus background service that rebuilds lost data and balances disk usage. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Customer concentration** — The share of a vendor's revenue that comes from its largest customers. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **CXL (Compute Express Link)** — An open interconnect that runs cache-coherent memory and I/O protocols over the PCIe physical layer. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **CXL memory** — DRAM attached over a Compute Express Link (PCIe-based) connection, adding capacity at roughly two to three times local DRAM latency. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **CXL Type 3 device** — A CXL memory expander: a controller plus DRAM that the host reaches with ordinary loads and stores. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **CXL.mem** — The CXL protocol that lets a host read and write a device's memory at cache-line granularity. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))

## D

- **D file server** — Colossus's simple network-attached disk server, read and written directly by the client library. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **3D NAND deck** — One separately etched section of a tall 3D NAND layer stack; high-layer parts stack two or three decks. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **3D XPoint** — The phase-change-based persistent memory technology behind Intel Optane, co-developed with Micron. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Dark site** — A customer installation that does not phone home, typically for security reasons, and therefore forgoes cloud analytics. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **DAS (direct-attached storage)** — Storage inside or cabled directly to one server, with no storage network in between. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **DASD (direct-access storage device)** — IBM's term for mainframe disk storage, as opposed to sequential tape. ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **DASE (disaggregated shared-everything)** — A storage architecture in which stateless compute nodes share access to all media in separate enclosures over an NVMe-oF fabric, so no node owns any data. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Data catalog** — An inventory of an organisation's datasets recording their schema, owner, classification and lineage. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Data catalog (table catalog)** — The service that maps table names to their current metadata pointer and enforces access, such as Unity Catalog or Apache Polaris. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Data curation** — Filtering, deduplicating, cleaning and tokenizing raw data into a training-ready dataset. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Data gravity** — The tendency of applications, services and spending to move toward where large volumes of data already sit. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Data lake** — A low-cost, usually object-based store that holds raw and curated data for analytics and AI. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Data lifecycle** — The progression of data from creation through active use, protection, cooling and archiving to deletion. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Data lineage** — The record of where data came from, how it was transformed and which outputs or decisions it fed. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Data loader** — The training-framework component that reads, decodes and prefetches batches of samples from storage for the GPUs. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Data node (EXA)** — a third-party Linux/NVMe server running Purity//DN that stores FlashBlade//EXA file data and serves it directly to clients. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **Data orchestration** — Policy-driven movement of files between tiers, sites and clouds without changing how applications address them. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Data plane** — The I/O path of a storage system that actually moves and protects bytes, which must keep running even if management services are unreachable. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Data Primacy** — Everpure's 2026 strategic framing that puts trusted, classified data rather than applications at the centre of the infrastructure stack. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Data reduction guarantee** — A vendor contract promising a minimum reduction ratio or effective capacity, usually on reducible data only, with extra capacity as the remedy. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Data retention** — How long NAND holds data without power before charge leakage causes errors; it shrinks as cells wear and as temperature rises. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Data security posture management (DSPM)** — Software that discovers and classifies sensitive data across an estate and flags where it is exposed or over-permissioned. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Data services** — The "intelligence" of a storage system: data placement, protection, data reduction and metadata management. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **Data stall** — Time a GPU waits for training data to be fetched from storage or pre-processed. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Data Stream** — Everpure's GPU-accelerated pipeline on FlashBlade that ingests, indexes and vectorises data for AI, based on NVIDIA's AI Data Platform design. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Data-in-place upgrade** — A controller hardware upgrade that leaves drives, data and configuration in place, so no migration is needed. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Data-loss incident log** — A vendor's record of every case of lost or corrupted customer data, with root cause and blast radius. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Data-on-MDT (DoM)** — A Lustre feature that stores the first part, or all, of small files on the metadata target to avoid a round trip to a data server. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md), [Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Data-parallel replica** — One full copy of the model in a data-parallel training job; replicas process different data and synchronize gradients. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Data-reduction ratio (DRR)** — Logical data stored divided by physical capacity consumed after deduplication and compression. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md), [Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Data-services breadth** — The range of enterprise data services (protocols, replication, ransomware recovery, cloud editions, consumption, cataloguing) delivered on the storage itself. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Datasheet sum vs. system result** — The difference between adding up per-box vendor ratings and measuring a whole configured system under a benchmark. ([Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **DBox** — VAST's storage enclosure holding SCM and QLC SSDs behind redundant DNodes. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **DBox-HA** — VAST's option that limits strips per enclosure so a cluster survives the loss of an entire DBox. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **DCQCN** — The standard ECN-based congestion-control algorithm for RoCEv2, in which the sender NIC cuts its rate on congestion notifications. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **DDN CORE** — DDN's control plane and data fabric, launched in November 2025, that spans EXAScaler and Infinia on-premises and in clouds. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **Deal archetype** — A recurring buyer profile, such as a neocloud training cluster or a sovereign HPC site, whose dominant requirement predicts which vendor wins. ([Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Declustered RAID** — Layout that scatters stripes and spare space across all drives in a pool so rebuilds run in parallel. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Decode** — The memory-bandwidth-bound inference phase that generates one token per step while rereading the weights and the full KV cache. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **Dedicated mode** — A deployment in which storage software runs on separate storage servers rather than on the compute nodes. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Deduplication** — Storing identical chunks of data once and replacing repeats with pointers found by fingerprint lookup. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Delegation** — An NFSv4 grant that lets one client cache a file exclusively until the server recalls it. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **Delta Lake** — Databricks-originated open table format that adds a transaction log to Parquet files in object storage. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Dennard scaling** — The historical rule that transistor power density stayed constant as transistors shrank, whose end around 2005 made chips power-limited. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Denominator question** — A follow-up that asks which population, period and exclusions sit behind a percentage or ratio. ([Ch 57](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/57-question-bank.md))
- **Dentry (directory entry)** — A record inside a directory that maps a file or subdirectory name to its inode number. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Depth label** — the atlas's three levels of understanding: L1 vocabulary, L2 mechanism and L3 implementation. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Design win** — A customer's commitment to build its platform around a supplier's technology, ahead of volume revenue. ([Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md), [Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **Design win (hyperscaler)** — A hyperscaler's commitment to build its storage on a supplier's technology, in Everpure's case licensed DirectFlash and Purity rather than finished arrays. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **DFMD** — An Everpure DirectFlash module with built-in NVRAM, so write-log capacity grows with the number of modules. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **DGX BasePOD** — NVIDIA's reference architecture for enterprise GPU clusters of two to dozens of DGX systems, with a list of validated storage partners. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **DGX SuperPOD** — NVIDIA's turnkey large-cluster reference architecture, built from scalable units, with storage certified against per-generation performance tables. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **Digital Omnibus on AI** — EU Regulation 2026/1744, which amended the AI Act and postponed its high-risk obligations to December 2027 and August 2028. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **DirectFlash** — Everpure's approach of letting Purity manage raw NAND directly instead of going through each SSD's own controller and FTL. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **DirectFlash licence** — Everpure's hyperscaler model in which the customer licenses DirectFlash software and design and sources its own NAND and hardware. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **DirectFlash Module (DFM)** — Everpure's proprietary flash module that exposes raw NAND through a thin controller, with no drive-level flash translation layer. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Directory bucket** — The S3 bucket type used by S3 Express One Zone, confined to one Availability Zone. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Disaggregated serving** — Running prefill and decode on separate GPU pools and transferring the KV cache between them. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **DiskANN** — Microsoft's SSD-resident graph vector index that keeps compressed codes in DRAM and the full graph and vectors on flash. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Distributed Namespace (DNE)** — Lustre's feature for spreading the namespace over multiple metadata targets, via remote directories and striped directories. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **DLIO** — the deep-learning I/O emulator MLPerf Storage uses to mimic framework data loading and to "sleep" in place of accelerator compute. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **DNA data storage** — Encoding digital data in synthesized DNA strands; extremely dense and durable but slow and costly to write. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **DNE (Distributed Namespace Environment)** — Lustre's mechanism for spreading a namespace across several metadata targets to relieve a single metadata server. ([Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **DNE (Distributed Namespace)** — Lustre's mechanism for spreading the namespace across several MDTs, via remote or striped directories. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **DNode** — VAST's enclosure fabric endpoint (often a DPU) that exposes an enclosure's SSDs to the NVMe-oF fabric. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Do-nothing option** — Continuing the current plan without new acquisitions or major partnerships, evaluated as a real alternative rather than a default. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Doorbell register** — A device register that the host writes to tell an NVMe controller that new queue entries are ready or have been consumed. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **DPDK (Data Plane Development Kit)** — A user-space networking library that lets software drive a NIC directly, bypassing the operating-system network stack. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **DPU (data processing unit)** — A NIC with its own general-purpose CPU complex and accelerators that can run storage, security or networking software. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **DSPM (data security posture management)** — Software that finds sensitive data across systems and checks who can access it. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Dual-controller array** — A scale-up storage system in which two controllers share dual-ported drives and each can take over the other's work if it fails. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Durability** — The property that acknowledged data survives failures and power loss without being lost or corrupted. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **DWPD (drive writes per day)** — An SSD endurance rating: how many times the drive's full capacity can be written each day over its warranty period. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Dynamic resharding** — Automatically increasing a bucket index's shard count as the object count grows, as Ceph RGW does above a per-shard threshold. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))

## E

- **E1.S** — A small EDSFF form factor suited to dense compute and GPU servers. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **E3.L** — A long EDSFF form factor with up to 70 W envelope, used for high-capacity QLC drives. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **East-west traffic** — Traffic between storage nodes, such as replicas, erasure-coded fragments, forwarded reads, rebalancing and rebuilds. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **EBox** — VAST's packaging that runs CNode and DNode software on the same server, trading independent scaling for hyperscaler and cloud fit. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md), [Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **ECN (Explicit Congestion Notification)** — Switches mark packets when queues build so senders can slow down before drops occur. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **EDSFF** — The SNIA family of data-centre SSD form factors (E1.S, E1.L, E3.S, E3.L) designed for density, airflow and scalable power. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Effective $/GB** — Storage price divided by logical capacity after data reduction, as opposed to raw or usable capacity. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Effective $/TB** — the price per terabyte a customer can actually store after data reduction, rather than per raw terabyte. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Effective capacity** — Usable capacity multiplied by an assumed data-reduction ratio. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md), [Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Effective training time** — The share of elapsed time that a training job spends doing useful training, after interruptions, restarts and checkpoint pauses. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md), [Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **elbencho** — an open-source distributed storage benchmark tool for file, object and GPU-direct testing. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **Element Store** — VAST's single metadata and data structure that represents files, objects, block volumes and tables as one kind of "element" underneath every protocol. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Embedding** — A fixed-length vector of numbers that represents the meaning of a piece of content so similar items can be found by vector search. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md), [Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Embodied carbon** — Greenhouse-gas emissions from manufacturing and shipping hardware, as distinct from emissions from powering it. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Enclosure blast radius** — The amount of data and service affected when an entire storage enclosure fails. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Enterprise Data Cloud (EDC)** — Everpure's 2025 architecture that uses Pure Fusion to manage a whole on-premises and cloud fleet as one policy-driven pool. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Enterprise level** — The middle NVIDIA-Certified Storage tier, simulating workloads of about 1,000 GPUs. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **Enterprise storage platform** — Gartner's category, created in 2025, covering products that serve block, file and object workloads together. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **Enterprise Storage Platforms (Gartner)** — Gartner's merged MQ category, from 2025, covering primary block plus file and object storage. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Entity List** — The US Commerce Department list of foreign parties subject to export licence requirements, which has included Huawei since 2019. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md), [Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Erasure coding (k+m)** — Scheme that stores k data strips plus m computed parity strips and can rebuild from any k of them. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Erasure set** — A fixed group of drives (2–16 in MinIO) across which one object's data and parity fragments are always written. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **ETag** — An identifier of an object's content or version, returned on writes and used for integrity checks and conditional requests. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Event Broker (VAST)** — VAST's Kafka-compatible event-streaming service, implemented as a protocol module so topics can be queried as tables. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Eventual consistency** — A guarantee only that all copies converge once writes stop, so reads in the meantime may be stale. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Ever Modern** — The Evergreen//Forever entitlement to new-generation controllers with each three-year subscription renewal (six years for //E products). ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **Evergreen** — Everpure's family of subscriptions (//Forever, //Flex, //One) that replaces periodic forklift array replacements with non-disruptive upgrades and consumption options. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **Evergreen//Flex** — Everpure's fleet-level program that bills capacity per use across a customer's arrays. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Evergreen//Forever** — Everpure's subscription for customer-owned arrays that includes in-place controller refreshes at each three-year renewal (formerly Evergreen Gold). ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Evergreen//One** — Everpure's storage-as-a-service offering (formerly Pure-as-a-Service), with SLAs on performance, availability, capacity and energy. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md), [Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **Evergreen//One for AI** — Everpure's storage-as-a-service offering for AI workloads, extended to FlashBlade//EXA in March 2026. ([Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Everpure** — the company formerly called Pure Storage, renamed in February 2026 and listed as NYSE: P since 2026-04-17. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md))
- **Everpure Cloud Azure Native** — Fully managed Everpure block storage delivered as an Azure Native ISV service, co-developed with Microsoft. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Everpure Cloud Dedicated** — Customer-managed Purity running in the customer's own AWS or Azure account; formerly Cloud Block Store. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Everpure Data Intelligence** — The data discovery, classification and semantic-context product built from the 1touch acquisition, GA in June 2026. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **Everpure Data Stream** — Everpure's GPU-accelerated ingest-to-inference data pipeline built on NVIDIA's AI Data Platform reference design. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **Everpure Platform** — Everpure's name for its whole software and hardware stack (Purity, arrays, Fusion, Pure1, Portworx, Everpure Cloud, Data Intelligence) sold as one platform. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **EXAScaler** — DDN's commercial distribution of the Lustre parallel file system, with management tooling, usually sold on DDN appliances. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **Extent** — A contiguous run of physical blocks described by a single map entry, replacing many per-block pointers. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Extent lock** — A distributed lock on a byte range of a file, letting several clients write different ranges of one file coherently. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **External enterprise storage systems** — Branded storage arrays sold as standalone systems to enterprises, the scope of IDC's headline quarterly storage tracker. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **External OEM ESS** — IDC's label for the external enterprise storage systems market, measured as vendor revenue by brand. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))

## F

- **Fabric amplification** — The ratio of back-end network traffic to client traffic, raised by mirroring and data migration. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Failover pair** — Two servers attached to the same dual-ported storage so either can take over the other's targets if one fails. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Failure domain** — A set of components that can fail together, such as a drive, node, enclosure, rack, power zone, site or region. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Fan-out** — Splitting one request into many parallel sub-requests, so that the slowest sub-request determines overall latency. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **FC-NVMe (NVMe/FC)** — The NVMe-oF transport that carries NVMe over Fibre Channel, standardized by INCITS T11 in 2017. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Federation** — Managing several arrays or controller pairs as one cluster with volume mobility, without merging them into one system. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Fibre Channel (FC)** — A dedicated, lossless storage network using credit-based flow control, the traditional enterprise SAN fabric. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Field failure data** — Measured failure rates and rebuild histories from deployed systems, as opposed to modelled reliability. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **File handle** — An opaque token issued by an NFS server that identifies a file in every subsequent request. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **File layout** — The map that tells a client which storage targets hold which parts of a file, including stripe size and stripe count. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **File storage** — Storage presented as a shared tree of named directories and files, with the file system run by the storage system. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Filer** — A dedicated network file-server appliance that does nothing but serve files over NFS or SMB (NetApp's original product). ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Fingerprint** — A cryptographic hash of a data chunk used as its identity in a deduplication index. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **fio** — the standard open-source I/O load generator used for vendor and customer storage tests, whose job file defines block size, queue depth and data pattern. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **First-party cloud storage service** — A partner's storage technology sold, supported and billed by a cloud provider as its own service (e.g., FSx for NetApp ONTAP). ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **FIT (failures in time)** — Failures per 10^9 device-hours; a 1% AFR is about 1,140 FIT. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Fixed-block chunking** — Cutting data into chunks at fixed offsets such as every 4 KB or 8 KB, which is cheap but misses duplicates after insertions shift the data. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Flash translation layer (FTL)** — SSD firmware that maps logical block addresses to physical NAND pages, so erase-before-write flash looks like a rewritable disk. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **FlashArray//C** — the QLC-based FlashArray that shares //X controllers and targets capacity-oriented tier-2 workloads. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashArray//E** — the QLC FlashArray tier aimed at replacing disk-based secondary and backup storage. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashArray//ST** — a latency-optimised, block-only FlashArray that uses commercial SSDs and switches off data reduction to shorten the I/O path. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashArray//X** — Everpure's mainstream TLC DirectFlash FlashArray for sub-millisecond tier-1 block and file workloads. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashArray//XL** — Everpure's highest-performance dual-controller FlashArray model for consolidated tier-0/1 block workloads. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashBlade//E** — the capacity-optimised FlashBlade with CPUs only in a control chassis and storage-only expansion chassis. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashBlade//EXA** — Everpure's AI/HPC system that splits a Purity//FB metadata core from separately scaled data nodes reached directly by pNFS clients. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashBlade//S** — Everpure's scale-out file and object performance tier built from blades and DirectFlash Modules. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **FlashCore Module** — IBM's custom flash module with in-module compression, used in FlashSystem arrays. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **FlashStack** — The Cisco and Everpure converged-infrastructure stack combining Cisco compute and networking with Everpure storage. ([Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **Flat namespace** — An addressing scheme with no real directories, where "folders" are only shared key prefixes. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Flex Files layout** — The pNFS layout type (RFC 8435, 2018) whose data servers can be ordinary NFSv3 servers and which supports client-side mirroring. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **Flexible Data Placement (FDP)** — An NVMe feature in which hosts tag writes with placement hints so data with similar lifetimes share erase blocks. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **FLIT** — The fixed 256-byte transfer unit of PCIe 6.0+ and CXL 3.x, carrying data plus FEC and CRC bytes. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Floor loading** — The weight per unit area a datacenter floor can bear, a limit on densely packed disk racks. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Flywheel** — A self-reinforcing loop in which early wins produce capital and references that make the next wins easier. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Foreign-investment review** — Government screening of cross-border acquisitions on national-security grounds, such as CFIUS in the United States. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Forever Flash** — Pure Storage's 2014 maintenance programme that bundled controller refreshes with maintenance renewals, the predecessor of Evergreen. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **Forklift upgrade** — Replacing an entire storage system and migrating its data, the incumbent refresh model that Evergreen was designed to remove. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Foundation level** — The entry NVIDIA-Certified Storage tier, testing workloads that simulate up to 128 GPUs. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **FoundationDB** — An open-source distributed transactional key-value database used as the metadata store by systems such as DeepSeek's 3FS and Snowflake. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Four-beat answer** — The structure of a 30-second explanation: what it is, why it matters, one number, and the implication for the company. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Front-end / back-end network** — In AI clusters, the north-south network for users, ingest and often storage, versus the east-west fabric for GPU-to-GPU traffic. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Front-end network** — The network that carries traffic between clients and storage nodes (north-south). ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md), [Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **3FS (Fire-Flyer File System)** — DeepSeek's open-source all-flash parallel file system for AI training and inference. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **FSx for Lustre** — AWS's managed Lustre parallel file system service, linked to S3. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **FTL mapping DRAM** — The DRAM an SSD uses to hold its logical-to-physical page map, roughly 1 GB per TB of flash at 4 KB granularity. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **Fusion preset** — A named, fleet-wide template in Everpure Fusion that bundles performance limits, protection policy and tags for provisioning workloads. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))

## G

- **Garbage collection (GC)** — Background work that copies valid pages out of partly stale blocks so the blocks can be erased and reused. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Gating requirement** — the one capability or certification without which a deal cannot close. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **GB/s per kW** — Storage bandwidth delivered per kilowatt of power, an efficiency metric suited to AI workloads. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **GDS compatibility mode** — The fallback in which cuFile calls still work but data passes through a host-memory bounce buffer because the platform or file system does not support the direct path. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Gemini (VAST)** — VAST Data's model in which customers buy certified hardware at cost from a partner and pay VAST a software subscription. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md), [Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **General availability (GA)** — the point at which a product is orderable and fully supported, though not necessarily feature-complete. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **Geo-distributed erasure coding** — Spreading an erasure-coded stripe across several sites so the loss of a whole site is survivable at lower capacity overhead than replication. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Global FTL** — a single flash translation layer that maps, garbage-collects and wear-levels across every flash module in an array rather than inside each drive. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Global namespace** — A single file tree that spans many storage systems, tiers and sites, so files keep one path wherever their bytes live. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Google Cloud Managed Lustre** — Google's first-party managed parallel file system service, built on DDN EXAScaler and generally available since July 2025. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **GPLv2** — The GNU General Public License version 2, a copyleft licence used by Lustre and the Linux kernel. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **GPU-initiated data access** — A data path in which GPU threads issue storage operations directly, without a CPU round-trip for each request. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **GPUDirect RDMA** — NVIDIA technology that lets a network card read or write GPU memory directly over PCIe, without copying through host memory. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **GPUDirect Storage (GDS)** — NVIDIA technology that lets storage data move by direct DMA between a NIC or NVMe SSD and GPU memory, bypassing the CPU bounce buffer. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Grace timer** — The wait before a missing node is declared failed, so a brief reboot triggers only a resync instead of a full rebuild. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Greedy garbage collection** — A GC policy that always reclaims the block with the fewest valid pages, minimising copies under random writes. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **GreenLake for File Storage** — HPE's file service built on VAST Data software running on Alletra MP hardware. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Grouped-query attention (GQA)** — An attention design in which several query heads share one key/value head, shrinking the KV cache per token. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))

## H

- **HA interconnect** — The dedicated link between two controllers that carries heartbeats and mirrored write data. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **HAMR** — heat-assisted magnetic recording, which briefly heats the platter with a laser so smaller, more stable magnetic grains can be written, raising HDD density. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md), [Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **HAMR (heat-assisted magnetic recording)** — HDD recording that briefly heats a tiny spot with a laser so that very stable, high-density magnetic media can be written. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Hard multi-tenancy** — Isolation of many customers' data, performance and administration on one shared system, enforced by the platform rather than by trust. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **Hardware compatibility list (HCL)** — The vendor-published list of servers, drives, NICs and firmware versions that software-defined storage is supported on. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Hardware-agnostic software** — Storage software sold to run on customer-chosen servers, GPU nodes or cloud instances rather than on vendor hardware. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Hashed (striped) directory** — A directory whose entries are spread across several metadata servers by hashing names. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **HBM (high-bandwidth memory)** — Stacked DRAM placed on the same package as a GPU or accelerator, the fastest and most expensive tier of the memory hierarchy. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **HCI (hyperconverged infrastructure)** — Running storage software on the same servers as the virtual machines, pooling their local drives. ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Head server** — The server that runs storage software in front of one or more JBOD enclosures. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Headline valuation multiple** — A private company's last valuation divided by its latest self-reported revenue or ARR figure; indicative only because definitions differ. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Headroom tax** — The capacity a redundant pair leaves unused so a single surviving controller can carry the full load. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Hedged read** — Requesting more fragments or replicas than needed and using the first to arrive, to cut tail latency. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md), [Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Hero configuration** — a benchmark system sized to win a headline rather than to match a realistic purchase. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **HHI (Herfindahl–Hirschman Index)** — A market-concentration measure equal to the sum of squared market shares; above 2,500 is usually treated as highly concentrated. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Hidden over-provisioning** — NAND capacity inside an SSD reserved for garbage collection and wear that the host can neither see nor use. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Hierarchical keyspace tenancy** — Multi-tenancy implemented by nesting tenants and datasets inside a key-value namespace, with a resource share assigned to each tenant. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **High-performance storage (HPS) certification** — NVIDIA's certification that a storage system meets the NCP reference architecture's fast-storage tier. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **High-risk AI system** — Under the EU AI Act, an AI system used in a listed sensitive area (such as hiring or credit) that must meet data-governance, logging and oversight obligations. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Hitachi iQ** — Hitachi Vantara's NVIDIA-based full-stack AI infrastructure offering built on VSP One storage. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **HNSW** — Hierarchical Navigable Small World, a multi-layer proximity-graph vector index that is fast in DRAM but needs one dependent memory access per hop. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Host Memory Buffer (HMB)** — An NVMe feature that lets a DRAM-less SSD borrow a slice of host memory to cache its mapping table. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Host-managed device memory (HDM)** — Device-attached memory mapped into the host's physical address space, typically exposed as a CPU-less NUMA node. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Hot / warm / cold data** — Labels for data by access frequency, from constantly accessed (hot) to rarely accessed (cold). ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Hot tier** — The high-performance file or flash storage tier that feeds GPUs directly during training and inference. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Hybrid bonding** — Joining separately made wafers (such as NAND arrays and their logic) face to face with direct copper connections. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI)** — An architecture in which every cluster node runs applications (usually VMs), storage software and local drives together. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Hyperscale commercial model** — Everpure's arrangement in which hyperscalers buy NAND themselves while Everpure supplies DirectFlash design, Purity software, support and some components. ([Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **Hyperscale licensing** — Everpure's business of licensing its DirectFlash design, software and support to hyperscalers that buy their own NAND. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md))
- **Hyperscaler licensing** — Everpure's model of licensing DirectFlash and Purity technology to hyperscalers, which buy their own NAND and hardware. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Hyperscaler self-build** — A hyperscaler designing its own storage software and buying commodity servers and drives instead of branded arrays. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Hyperscaler-native storage** — Storage services built and run by AWS, Azure or Google themselves, such as S3, Blob and GCS. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **HyperStore** — Cloudian's S3-native object storage software and appliance line. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))

## I

- **IBM FlashCore Module** — IBM's proprietary flash module for FlashSystem that keeps an in-module FTL and adds compression, encryption and threat detection. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
