- **IBM Storage Scale (GPFS)** — IBM's parallel file system, shipped since 1998 and renamed from Spectrum Scale in 2022, which distributes metadata management across nodes using tokens. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Illustrative chart** — a chart of modelled rather than measured data, labelled "Illustrative" in its title. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **ILM (information lifecycle management)** — NetApp StorageGRID's rule engine that decides where and how (replicated or erasure-coded) each object is stored over time. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **IMFT (IM Flash Technologies)** — The Intel–Micron NAND (later 3D XPoint) manufacturing joint venture in Lehi, Utah, formed in 2006 and unwound in 2019. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Incast** — Many senders converging on one receiver port at once, the typical overload pattern in storage networks. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Incumbent (storage)** — An established storage vendor with a large installed base and broad portfolio, such as Dell, NetApp, HPE, IBM, Hitachi Vantara or Huawei. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Indirection unit** — the granularity at which an SSD's mapping table tracks data; larger units save DRAM but penalise small random writes. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Indirection unit (IU)** — The granularity at which an SSD's mapping table tracks data; larger units save DRAM but penalise smaller writes. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Inference Context Memory Storage (ICMS)** — NVIDIA's CES 2026 name for its BlueField-4-powered KV-cache storage tier, later delivered as CMX. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **Infinia** — DDN's software-defined data platform, built on a distributed key-value store, that serves S3, SDK, KV-cache and limited POSIX access. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **InfiniBand** — A purpose-built, credit-based lossless network fabric for HPC and AI, today supplied effectively only by NVIDIA (Quantum). ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **InfiniBox** — Infinidat's high-end block array that serves most reads from DRAM in front of large media pools; now part of Lenovo. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Infrastructure as code (IaC)** — Managing infrastructure through declarative, version-controlled definitions applied by tools such as Terraform or Ansible. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Initiator** — The host side of a block-storage session that issues read and write commands. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Inline object** — A small object whose bytes are stored inside its metadata record instead of being erasure-coded into separate fragments. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Inline reduction** — Data reduction performed before data is written to persistent media. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Innovator's dilemma** — The pattern in which incumbents rationally serve their best customers and miss a new segment that later becomes the growth market. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Inode** — A per-file record holding a file's attributes (owner, permissions, size, timestamps) and pointers to where its data lives. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Integrated media moat** — a competitive advantage from owning flash management down to the media, as with DirectFlash. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md))
- **Integrated memory controller** — a DRAM controller built onto the CPU die instead of a separate northbridge chip; the analogy for moving flash control into array software. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Integration seam** — One of the places an acquired product must join the acquirer: control plane, data path, licensing or channel. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **IntelliFlash** — The all-flash array line (ex-Tegile) that DDN bought from Western Digital in 2019. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **Interleaving** — Mixing topics within one review session instead of drilling one topic at a time. ([Ch 59](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/59-self-test-flashcards.md))
- **io2 Block Express** — AWS's highest-performance EBS volume type, built on a re-architected back end reached over SRD. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **IO500** — A twice-yearly ranking of HPC storage systems, started at SC17, that combines bandwidth and metadata scores via geometric means. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md), [Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **IO500 Production list** — the IO500 list restricted to submissions that pass a reproducibility review, separate from the Research list for experimental systems. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **IOPS** — Input/output operations completed per second, usually quoted for small (4 KiB) random reads. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **IOPS per TB** — A device's or system's random IOPS divided by its capacity; the metric that falls as hard drives grow. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **ior-easy / ior-hard** — IO500 bandwidth tests: large, well-aligned sequential I/O versus small, unaligned I/O to a shared file. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **iSCSI** — SCSI commands carried over TCP/IP on ordinary Ethernet (IETF RFC 3720, 2004). ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **ISG (Infrastructure Solutions Group)** — Dell's reporting segment that contains servers, networking and storage. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Issue fingerprint** — A telemetry signature of a known fault that a vendor matches across its connected fleet to prevent recurrences. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **IVF (inverted file index)** — A vector index that clusters vectors and searches only the few clusters nearest the query. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))

## J

- **JBOD** — "Just a bunch of disks": a drive enclosure with no storage controller logic, attached to a separate head server. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))

## K

- **Kernel bypass** — Moving data between an application and the NIC without system calls, interrupts or kernel socket buffers on the data path. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md), [Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Key-person risk** — Dependence on a few people, often core code authors, whose departure would stall the product. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Kingmaker risk** — Dependence on a platform owner, such as NVIDIA, whose endorsements can be extended to rivals at any time. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Kioxia** — The NAND maker formerly called Toshiba Memory, sold to a Bain-led consortium in 2018 and listed in Tokyo in December 2024. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **KubeVirt** — Open-source project that runs virtual machines as Kubernetes objects, a common VMware-exit path. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **KV cache** — The per-token attention keys and values an LLM stores during inference so it does not recompute them for each new token. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md), [Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **KV-cache offload** — Storing a transformer's key/value tensors outside GPU memory so that a repeated prompt prefix can be reloaded instead of recomputed. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **KVBM (KV Block Manager)** — The Dynamo component that tiers KV-cache blocks across GPU memory, host DRAM, local SSD and remote storage. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md), [Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))

## L

- **L1 (vocabulary)** — the depth at which you can define a term and use it correctly in a sentence. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **L1 / L2 card** — A flashcard that tests vocabulary (L1) or mechanism and trade-off (L2), matching the atlas's depth labels. ([Ch 59](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/59-self-test-flashcards.md))
- **L2 (mechanism)** — the atlas's default depth: you can whiteboard how something works, name its trade-offs and say why one design wins for a workload. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **L3 (implementation)** — code paths, on-disk formats and kernel internals, covered only as pointers in "Going deeper" boxes. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **L4 cache** — Colossus's machine-learning-driven tier that decides which data is cached or written to SSD instead of HDD. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Lakehouse** — An architecture that runs warehouse-style SQL and AI workloads directly on open file and table formats in object storage. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Lance** — An open columnar file format, created by LanceDB's founders, designed for both scans and fast random row access to embeddings and multimodal data. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Land motion** — the first product sold into a new account, intended to lead to expansion. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **Latency** — The time from issuing one storage request to its completion, measured in microseconds for flash and milliseconds for disk. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Latency adder** — The extra time per I/O that a transport or software layer adds on top of the storage device itself. ([Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **Latency-bound workload** — A workload whose performance depends on how quickly each small I/O completes, such as an OLTP database. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **Layout** — The pNFS map telling a client which data servers hold which byte ranges of a file and how they are striped. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **LBA (logical block address)** — The number that identifies one fixed-size block within a block volume. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **LDPC (low-density parity-check) code** — The strong error-correcting code that modern SSD controllers apply to every NAND read. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Lease** — A time-bounded grant of state (opens, locks) that an NFSv4 client must keep renewing or lose. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **Leitner box** — A paper spaced-repetition system in which correctly answered cards move to less frequently reviewed boxes and missed cards return to the first box. ([Ch 59](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/59-self-test-flashcards.md))
- **Lifecycle policy** — A rule that automatically expires, deletes old versions of, or moves objects to another tier after a set age or condition. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Lightning File System** — Dell's parallel file system for AI workloads, built on OneFS foundations and previewed as Project Lightning. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Linearizability (strong consistency)** — A guarantee that every read sees the latest acknowledged write, as if only one copy existed. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Listen-for note** — A one-line description of what a strong answer to a question should contain. ([Ch 57](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/57-question-bank.md))
- **Little's law** — The queueing identity L = λW: requests in flight equal arrival rate times time in system, so outstanding I/Os = IOPS × latency. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **llm-d** — An open-source, Kubernetes-native distributed inference project (CNCF Sandbox) with KV-aware scheduling and offload. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **LMCache** — An open-source KV-cache layer that offloads and shares KV between inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang and storage tiers. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **LNet** — Lustre's network layer, which carries traffic over RDMA fabrics such as InfiniBand and RoCE or over TCP and can route between them. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Local checkpointing** — Writing each node's checkpoint shard to its own SSD or RAM disk and replicating it to peer nodes before or instead of writing to shared storage. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Locally decodable code** — An erasure code that can rebuild a lost strip by reading only a subset of the stripe, cutting rebuild I/O. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Locally decodable erasure code (LDEC)** — VAST's wide erasure code that can rebuild a lost strip by reading only a fraction (about a quarter) of the stripe. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Log-on-log** — Stacking a log-structured array on top of SSDs that are themselves log-structured, duplicating garbage collection, spare space and mapping. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md), [Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Log-structured design** — A storage design that appends every change to a log and garbage-collects old versions instead of updating in place. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Logical-to-physical (L2P) table** — The FTL's map from each logical address to its current physical NAND location, usually held in on-drive DRAM. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Long-term agreement (LTA)** — a multi-year memory supply contract, increasingly with prepayments and price floors and ceilings. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **LOTA (Local Object Transport Accelerator)** — CoreWeave's cache on each GPU node's local NVMe that accelerates reads from its AI Object Storage. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **LTO (Linear Tape-Open)** — The dominant open tape-cartridge standard; LTO-10 holds 30 TB native per cartridge. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **LUN (logical unit number)** — The SCSI address of a block volume presented by a target. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **LUN (logical unit)** — A block volume that a storage array presents to a host as if it were a disk. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Lustre** — The open-source parallel file system that runs most of the world's largest supercomputers, now developed mainly by DDN's Whamcloud unit and the community. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))

## M

- **Magic Quadrant (MQ)** — Gartner's annual vendor assessment plotting ability to execute against completeness of vision; a perception signal, not market share. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Magnum IO** — NVIDIA's umbrella name for its GPU input/output software, including GPUDirect RDMA, GPUDirect Storage, NCCL, NVSHMEM and UCX. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Management plane** — A fleet-wide layer, often vendor-hosted in the cloud, that aggregates many arrays' control planes for monitoring, analytics and policy. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** — An open protocol that lets AI agents connect to tools and data sources, now exposed by several storage management planes. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **MCP server** — A service that exposes tools and data to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol, here used to let agents query and act on storage fleets. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md), [Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **MDS (metadata server)** — The server in a parallel file system that handles namespace operations and hands out file layouts and locks. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **MDT (metadata target)** — The storage volume behind a Lustre MDS that holds directories, inodes, permissions and file layouts. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **mdtest** — The metadata benchmark used in IO500, measuring create, stat, read and delete rates in private (easy) and shared (hard) directories. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md), [Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **Mean time between failures (MTBF)** — The average time a system or job runs between failures; for large training jobs it shrinks roughly in proportion to GPU count. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Media economics** — the cost, density and power advantages a vendor gets from how it manages flash media, not from the NAND price itself. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md), [Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Mediator** — Third-party witness that decides which side of a partitioned metro cluster keeps serving I/O. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Memory cycle** — The recurring boom-bust pattern in which high memory prices fund new capacity that later overshoots demand and crashes prices. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Memory pooling** — Assigning slices of switch-attached memory to different hosts on demand to reduce stranded DRAM. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Memory–storage wall** — The roughly 1,000× latency jump between DRAM-class memory (~100 ns) and NAND flash (~100 µs) that storage-system design works to hide. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Metadata** — Data about stored data: names, directory structure, permissions, sizes, timestamps and the maps from file offsets to physical blocks. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Metadata bucket** — In WEKA, one of thousands of hashed shards of the file-system namespace, each owned by a virtual metadata server. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Metadata core** — in FlashBlade//EXA, the FlashBlade blades running Purity//FB that hold the namespace, layouts and locks. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md), [Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Metadata index (object store)** — The replicated, sharded table that maps each bucket, key and version to an object's size, ETag and fragment locations. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Metadata pyramid** — Everpure's term for Purity's tiered metadata store, with hot entries in DRAM, in-flight changes in NVRAM and the bulk on flash. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Metadata server (MDS)** — The server or service that owns namespace and inode operations in a file system whose data lives elsewhere. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Metadata storm** — A burst of creates, opens or stats, such as thousands of ranks writing checkpoint files at once, that saturates the metadata tier. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Metadata/data split** — A design that scales metadata servers separately from data nodes, with clients reading data nodes directly, as in pNFS or Lustre. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md), [Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md), [Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **MGS (management server)** — The Lustre server that stores cluster configuration, which clients read when they mount the file system. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Migration (SCM-to-QLC)** — The background process that reduces buffered data and writes it to QLC flash in large erasure-coded stripes. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Mirrored write cache** — A design in which each write is copied to the partner controller's persistent memory before the host is acknowledged. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Mixed-precision training** — Training that computes in low precision (bf16 or FP8) while keeping fp32 master weights and optimizer state for numerical stability. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Mixed-version cluster** — a cluster temporarily running two software releases during a rolling upgrade. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Mixture of experts (MoE)** — A model design that activates only some of its parameters per token, so compute follows active parameters while checkpoint size follows total parameters. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **MLPerf Storage** — MLCommons' benchmark that measures how well a storage system feeds AI workloads using software-simulated accelerators instead of real GPUs. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md), [Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **MLPerf Storage checkpointing workload** — an MLCommons test that measures how fast a storage system writes and reads emulated LLM training checkpoints. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **MLPerf Storage KV-cache workload** — an MLCommons v3.0 test that measures how fast storage can deliver inference context (KV cache) to emulated accelerators. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** — Open protocol, introduced by Anthropic in 2024 and now governed under the Linux Foundation, that standardises how AI agents discover and call external tools and data sources. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Model FLOPs utilization (MFU)** — The fraction of a GPU's peak arithmetic throughput a training job actually uses on model math. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Monotonic write** — a write that only ever appends new data or records and never modifies existing ones in place. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Mountpoint for Amazon S3** — AWS's open-source file client that maps file reads and writes to S3 requests. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Mozaic** — Seagate's family of HAMR disk platforms, named by terabytes per platter (Mozaic 3+, 4+, 5). ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **MTTDL (mean time to data loss)** — A modelled estimate of how long a protection scheme runs before enough overlapping failures lose data. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Multi-head latent attention (MLA)** — DeepSeek's attention design that caches a compressed latent vector per layer instead of full keys and values, cutting KV size several-fold. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **Multipart upload** — An S3 method for uploading a large object as many parallel, independently retryable parts that become visible atomically on completion. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Multipath I/O (MPIO)** — Host software that spreads I/O over several paths to an array and fails over between them. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))

## N

- **Nameplate power** — The rated maximum power of a device or power supply, usually well above its typical draw. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Namespace** — The NVMe equivalent of a LUN, an addressable block volume exposed by an NVMe controller. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md), [Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **NAND flash** — A flash memory architecture with cells wired in series strings, trading random-read speed for much higher density and lower cost per bit. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **NAND pass-through** — How quickly and fully changes in NAND cost are reflected in a storage vendor's selling prices. ([Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **NAND qualification** — characterising a new NAND die (read thresholds, retention, program timing) so firmware or software can drive it reliably. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **NAND string** — A column of NAND cells connected in series along one vertical channel between a bit line and a source line. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **NAS (network-attached storage)** — A storage system that owns the file system and serves files to hosts over NFS or SMB. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **NCCL** — NVIDIA's library for collective communication (such as all-reduce) between GPUs within and across servers. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **nconnect** — A Linux NFS mount option (kernel 5.3+) that opens up to 16 TCP connections per mount to the same server. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **NCP (NVIDIA Cloud Partner)** — NVIDIA's programme, requirements and reference designs for GPU cloud providers, including a storage certification tier. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **Near-synchronous replication** — Continuous streaming replication with local acknowledgement, giving an RPO of seconds. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Nearline HDD** — high-capacity 7,200 rpm hard drives used for warm and cold data in data centres. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **NeMo Retriever** — NVIDIA microservices that extract, embed and rerank enterprise data for retrieval-augmented generation. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **Neocloud** — A GPU-specialist cloud provider that rents AI clusters (bare metal, Kubernetes or Slurm) to labs, enterprises and hyperscalers, e.g. CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md), [Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Net dollar retention (NDR)** — Recurring revenue from an existing customer cohort this year as a percentage of the same cohort's revenue a year earlier. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md), [Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md), [Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **NeuralMesh** — WEKA's software-defined storage platform since June 2025, the re-architected successor to WekaFS and the WEKA Data Platform. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **NeuralMesh 6** — WEKA's July 2026 platform release adding multi-tenancy, always-on data reduction and native object access. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **NeuralMesh Axon** — WEKA's packaging of NeuralMesh to run inside GPU servers on their local NVMe drives and spare CPU cores. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Neutrality** — A vendor's ability to serve data stored on rivals' systems, which partners and multi-vendor buyers value. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **NFS (Network File System)** — The standard file-sharing protocol on Linux and Unix, in which clients send file-level operations to a server that owns the file system. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **NFS over RDMA** — NFS carried over RPC-over-RDMA (RFC 8166/8267), letting servers place data directly in client memory with little CPU involvement. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **NFSv3** — The stateless 1995 version of NFS (RFC 1813), still the most widely deployed, with locking handled by separate side protocols. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **NFSv4.1** — The NFS minor version (RFC 5661, now RFC 8881) that added sessions, trunking and parallel NFS (pNFS). ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **NFSv4.2** — The NFS minor version (RFC 7862, 2016) that added server-side copy, sparse files, I/O hints and labeled NFS. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **NIM** — NVIDIA Inference Microservices, packaged containers that serve AI models behind standard APIs. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **Nitro card** — AWS's custom offload card that, among other jobs, presents EBS volumes to guests as NVMe devices and sends I/O over the network. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **NIXL (NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library)** — An open-source library that moves KV-cache blocks and tensors between GPU memory, CPU memory and storage through pluggable backends. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md), [Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **NKP** — Nutanix Kubernetes Platform, built from the D2iQ acquisition and launched in 2024. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **No-regret move** — A strategic action that pays off across almost all plausible scenarios. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Non-disruptive upgrade (NDU)** — Upgrading array software or controller hardware one controller at a time so hosts keep running. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md), [Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **NOR flash** — A flash memory architecture with cells wired in parallel, giving fast random reads at low density; used mainly for code storage. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **NQN (NVMe Qualified Name)** — The unique name identifying an NVMe host or subsystem for discovery and access control. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Nutanix Unified Storage (NUS)** — Nutanix's software storage offering covering Files, Objects and Volumes on its platform. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **NVIDIA AI Data Platform** — NVIDIA's 2025 reference design for putting GPUs, DPUs and NVIDIA retrieval software inside storage systems. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **NVIDIA Cloud Partner (NCP)** — NVIDIA's program and reference architectures for GPU cloud providers, including storage uptime, durability and delivery requirements. ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **NVIDIA Dynamo** — NVIDIA's open-source distributed inference-serving framework that routes requests and manages KV cache across GPUs and memory tiers. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md), [Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **NVIDIA STX** — NVIDIA's BlueField-4-based storage reference architecture launched at GTC 2026. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **NVIDIA-Certified Storage (NVCS)** — NVIDIA's storage certification programme with Foundation, Enterprise and NCP levels for AI factory deployments. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md), [Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **NVL72** — NVIDIA's rack-scale system joining 72 Blackwell GPUs by NVLink into one liquid-cooled rack drawing roughly 120–130 kW. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **NVMe** — A storage interface and command set designed for flash on PCIe, built around many parallel submission and completion queues. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF)** — The extension of NVMe across a network, using command and response capsules over RDMA, Fibre Channel or TCP. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **NVMe/RoCE** — NVMe-oF over RDMA on converged Ethernet, in which the target moves data directly to or from host memory without CPU copies. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **NVMe/TCP** — The NVMe-oF transport that carries capsules and data on ordinary TCP connections, ratified in 2018. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **NVRAM** — Non-volatile memory in a storage controller that holds acknowledged writes until they are written to flash, surviving power loss. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **NVRAM write log** — A small battery-, capacitor- or flash-backed persistent buffer that holds acknowledged writes until they are flushed to flash. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))

## O

- **Object** — An immutable blob of bytes plus metadata, stored and retrieved whole by key through an API such as S3. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Object gateway** — A stateless server that terminates S3 requests, checks authentication and policy, and reads or writes object fragments on behalf of clients. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Object key** — The string name that addresses an object in a bucket's flat namespace; slashes in it are just characters. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md), [Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Object storage** — Storage presented as flat buckets of objects, each with a key, data and metadata, accessed whole over HTTP APIs such as S3. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **ObjectEngine** — Pure Storage's short-lived backup appliance built on StorReduce deduplication technology, launched in 2019 and de-emphasised by mid-2020. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **OceanStor A-series** — Huawei's AI-oriented scale-out storage line, led by the A800. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **OceanStor M900** — Huawei's context-memory storage system for sharing KV cache across inference clusters. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **ODM direct** — Storage or server hardware built by an original design manufacturer to a hyperscaler's own design and sold to it directly, bypassing branded OEMs. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Office of the CTO** — the group that frames long-horizon technology bets, standards engagement and external technical strategy. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **On-behalf-of authorisation** — Access control in which an agent's effective rights are the intersection of the delegating user's rights and the agent's own scope. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **One-liner** — A 30-second, plain-English answer that states what something is, why it matters and at most one sourced number. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **One-page map** — the atlas's mindmap of the storage and AI-storage domain, from media to Everpure. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md))
- **Open division** — the MLPerf category that allows disclosed changes to loaders, formats or frameworks, so results are not directly comparable with closed ones. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **Open Semantic Interchange (OSI)** — A Snowflake-initiated, multi-vendor open specification for exchanging semantic-layer definitions, first published in January 2026. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Open-channel SSD** — an SSD that exposes NAND geometry to the host so host software performs flash management, the precursor of zoned and placement-hint designs. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Open-core relicensing** — Narrowing or restricting a free open-source edition to push users toward paid commercial editions. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Operating lease** — Financing in which a lessor owns the hardware and the customer pays periodic rent, recorded under ASC 842 as a right-of-use asset and lease liability. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **Operational carbon** — Emissions from the electricity a system consumes over its service life. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Optimizer state** — The per-parameter values an optimizer such as Adam keeps (fp32 master weights and two moment estimates), which make up most of a checkpoint's size. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **OSD (object storage daemon)** — The Ceph process that manages one drive and stores, replicates and recovers its objects. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **OSS (object storage server)** — The Lustre server that serves file data from its object storage targets. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **OST (object storage target)** — A Lustre data volume, usually a RAID-protected local file system, that stores file data as objects. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Over-provisioning (OP)** — Flash installed in a drive but hidden from the host, used as working space for garbage collection, expressed as a percentage of user capacity. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Overall response time (ORT)** — SPECstorage's average latency across the load points of a run. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))

## P

- **P/E cycle** — One program/erase cycle of a NAND block; the unit in which flash wear and endurance are counted. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **p99 / p99.9** — The latency that 1% or 0.1% of requests exceed. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **PACELC** — An extension of CAP: under a Partition choose Availability or Consistency, Else choose Latency or Consistency. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Packaging** — how features are bundled into SKUs, tiers and contracts. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **PagedAttention** — vLLM's technique of storing KV cache in fixed-size pages, like virtual memory, to cut fragmentation and enable block sharing. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **PAM4** — Four-level pulse-amplitude modulation, carrying two bits per symbol to double lane rates over NRZ. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md), [Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Parallel file system** — A file system in which clients get a file's layout from metadata servers and then read and write its data directly and in parallel across many storage servers. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Partitioned prefix** — The key-prefix unit by which S3 scales request throughput, each supporting at least 3,500 writes and 5,500 reads per second. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Partitioned-writer** — Everpure's term for the FlashBlade design in which blades own slices of the namespace while flash is managed globally. ([Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **Pass-through lag** — the delay between a change in component cost and the matching change in a vendor's selling prices. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Pattern removal** — Detecting all-zero or repeating-pattern blocks and recording them as metadata instead of storing them. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Paxos** — Lamport's majority-based consensus protocol, published in 1998 and used in systems such as Ceph monitors and DynamoDB. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Payback period** — The years of incremental gross profit or cash flow needed to recover a purchase price. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **PB per rack** — Raw or usable petabytes held in one rack, limited in practice by rack power, cooling and floor loading. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Peer-to-peer DMA** — A transfer in which one PCIe device (such as a NIC) writes directly into another device's memory (such as a GPU) without involving host memory. ([Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **Performance density** — Storage throughput or GPUs fed per rack unit or per kilowatt, the metric DDN emphasises in benchmarks. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **Performance HDD** — 10K and 15K RPM enterprise hard drives optimised for IOPS rather than capacity, largely displaced by flash. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Persistence point** — The layer at which a write is durable enough for the system to acknowledge it, typically mirrored NVRAM in an array or power-loss-protected DRAM in an SSD. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **Persona** — the specific buyer or operator a product is designed and priced for, such as a VMware admin or an AI platform team. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **PFC (Priority Flow Control)** — An Ethernet mechanism that pauses a link for one traffic class to prevent drops, at the risk of spreading congestion. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Phone-home telemetry** — Outbound metrics, logs and health data that an array sends to its vendor's cloud for support and analytics. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Physalia** — AWS's configuration-master store for EBS, giving each volume its own small Paxos-replicated cell. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Placeholder score** — A neutral score assigned in a scorecard where public data is silent, flagged for diligence access. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Placement group (PG)** — Ceph's unit of placement and rebalancing, grouping many objects that are mapped together to the same set of drives. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **PLC (penta-level cell)** — NAND flash storing 5 bits per cell in 32 voltage states; denser than QLC but slower and less durable. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **pNFS (parallel NFS)** — An NFSv4.1+ feature in which a metadata server hands clients a layout so they can read and write data servers directly and in parallel. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **pNFS Flex Files** — The NFSv4.2 parallel-NFS layout that lets clients do I/O directly against data servers after getting a layout from a metadata server. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **pNFS layout** — the map a pNFS metadata server returns telling a client which data servers hold which parts of a file. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **Policy decision point** — The component that evaluates an access request against policy and returns allow, deny or mask. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **Portworx** — Everpure's software-defined data-services layer that gives Kubernetes containers and VMs persistent storage, replication, backup and DR on any infrastructure. ([Ch 28](docs/04-everpure/28-platform-and-software.md))
- **POSIX semantics** — The Unix file-system behaviour (open, read, write, rename, byte-range locks, immediate visibility) that applications assume of a local disk. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **Post-process reduction** — Data reduction performed in the background after data has landed on media. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Post-training** — Training steps after pre-training, such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, that adapt a base model. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Power-limited datacenter** — A facility whose output is bounded by available electricity rather than by chip supply or floor space. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Power-loss protection (PLP)** — On-drive capacitors that hold up power long enough to flush buffered writes and map updates after a power failure. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md), [Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **Powered shell** — A datacenter building with grid power and cooling in place, ready for IT equipment to be installed. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **Pre-election** — Everpure ActiveCluster behaviour that pre-selects a surviving array per pod when both arrays lose contact with the mediator. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Prefetching** — Fetching data into a faster tier before it is requested so that the consumer never waits on the slower tier. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Prefill** — The compute-bound inference phase that processes the whole prompt in parallel and produces the KV cache. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **Prefix caching** — Reusing stored KV blocks for the identical leading tokens (system prompt, document, earlier turns) shared by many requests. ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **Prepayment (supplier)** — cash paid to a component maker before delivery to secure allocation, recorded as a prepaid asset rather than inventory. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Preset (Pure Fusion)** — A fleet-wide template bundling capacity, QoS, protection and tags that Fusion uses to provision a workload consistently. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Price collar** — a contract term that sets both a floor and a ceiling on the price paid, limiting both upside and downside. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Price pass-through** — revenue growth that comes from passing higher component (NAND) costs on to customers rather than from shipping more units. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md))
- **Price-led growth** — Revenue growth driven by higher component (mainly NAND) prices passed through to customers rather than by more units or capacity shipped. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Price/volume decomposition** — Splitting revenue growth into change in price per unit (e.g., per TB) and change in units shipped. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Primary OSD** — The OSD that receives a placement group's writes, forwards them to replicas and acknowledges the client. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Primary storage** — The tier that serves live applications and is optimised for latency, performance and availability. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Product gross margin** — Gross profit on hardware and licence (product) revenue as a percentage of that revenue. ([Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **Product quantization (PQ)** — Compressing a vector by splitting it into sub-vectors and replacing each with a small codebook index, cutting memory by tens of times. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Program/erase asymmetry** — NAND's property that data is programmed page by page but can only be erased a whole (much larger) block at a time, so it cannot be overwritten in place. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Progressive File Layout (PFL)** — A Lustre feature that widens a file's stripe count automatically as the file grows. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Project Silica** — Microsoft's research program for archival data storage written by laser into quartz or borosilicate glass. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Proof of concept (PoC)** — A hands-on test of a vendor's system on the buyer's own workloads, ideally on the buyer's hardware. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Proprietary parallel client** — A vendor kernel module or agent that stripes I/O directly across storage servers, as in Lustre, IBM Storage Scale or WEKA. ([Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **Protection level (OneFS)** — PowerScale's notation for how many drive or node failures a file can survive, e.g., +2d:1n. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Protocol family** — The three ways a host sees storage: as a disk (block), a directory tree (file) or a bucket of keys (object). ([Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **PUE (power usage effectiveness)** — Total facility power divided by IT equipment power; 1.0 would mean zero cooling and distribution overhead. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Pull-forward demand** — Orders placed earlier than needed to beat expected price increases, which inflates current growth and borrows from future quarters. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Pure Fusion** — Everpure's policy-driven fleet control plane, embedded in Purity, that provisions workloads across FlashArray, FlashBlade and cloud arrays. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Pure Storage Cloud Dedicated** — Everpure's customer-managed Purity block service on AWS and Azure, formerly Cloud Block Store. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **Pure1** — Everpure's SaaS monitoring, analytics and support portal fed by array phone-home telemetry. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **PureKVA** — Everpure's KV-cache offload software on FlashBlade (formerly Key Value Accelerator), serving cached LLM attention state over S3 and NFS. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md), [Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md), [Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md), [Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))
- **Purity** — Everpure's storage operating system for FlashArray (Purity//FA) and FlashBlade (Purity//FB), built as a log-structured, metadata-centric design. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **Purity DeepReduce** — Everpure's similarity-based, cluster-wide, asynchronous data reduction for FlashBlade, introduced in 2026. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Purity Turbo** — An Everpure feature for FlashArray//XL190 that lets the secondary controller serve read I/O. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md), [Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **Purity//DN** — Everpure's data-node software for FlashBlade//EXA, running on off-the-shelf servers. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md), [Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md), [Ch 45](docs/06-industry-and-competition/45-head-to-head.md))

## Q

- **Quadrant chart** — A two-axis chart split into four labelled quadrants, used to group vendors by two strategic dimensions. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Qualification matrix** — The set of server, NIC, drive, kernel and cloud combinations a software vendor must test and support. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Question bank** — A curated, numbered set of questions tagged by topic and audience, used to prepare for internal meetings. ([Ch 57](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/57-question-bank.md))
- **Queue depth** — The number of I/O requests outstanding at a device or system at one time. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Queue pair** — The send/receive work-queue pair through which an application posts RDMA operations directly to the NIC. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Quorum** — The majority of voting members (e.g., 3 of 5 monitors) required to change cluster state, which prevents split brain. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Quorum (N/W/R)** — The replica count N and the number of write (W) and read (R) acknowledgements required; W + R > N ensures reads overlap the latest write. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))

## R

- **R-generation** — a FlashArray or FlashBlade controller refresh (for example R4, R5) that Evergreen customers can apply in place without migrating data. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **R2T (Ready to Transfer)** — A target's message inviting the host to send write data, used in iSCSI and NVMe/TCP. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Raft** — A consensus protocol (2014) designed to be easy to understand, with leader election by term and majority-committed log replication. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)** — Answering a prompt by first retrieving relevant documents from an index and feeding them to the model as context. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md), [Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **RAID (redundant array of inexpensive disks)** — Combining many cheap drives with mirroring or parity so the group is faster and more reliable than any one drive. ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **RAID 1 (mirroring)** — Protection scheme that writes every block to two drives, giving 50% usable capacity. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **RAID 10** — Striping across mirrored pairs; 50% usable capacity with fast, simple rebuilds. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **RAID 5** — Striping with one rotating parity block per stripe; survives one drive failure. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **RAID 6** — Striping with two independent parity blocks (P and Q) per stripe; survives any two drive failures. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **RAID-HA** — Purity's dual-parity data protection scheme across flash modules. ([Ch 26](docs/04-everpure/26-purity-and-directflash.md))
- **RAMAC** — IBM's 1956 305 computer and its 350 disk unit, the first commercial hard disk system (about 3.75 MB). ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Rapid Bucket** — Google Cloud's zonal Cloud Storage bucket on Colossus aimed at AI workloads (formerly Rapid Storage). ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Ratable revenue** — Revenue recognised evenly over a service period rather than at shipment. ([Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **Ratable revenue recognition** — Recognizing revenue evenly over the service period rather than upfront at delivery. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **Raw capacity** — The sum of the drives' capacities in decimal terabytes, before any protection or overhead. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Raw, usable and effective capacity** — Capacity before data protection, after protection, and after an assumed data-reduction ratio; vendors' prices differ by which one they quote. ([Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **RBD** — RADOS Block Device, Ceph's block storage interface. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **RDMA (remote direct memory access)** — A transport in which the network card moves data directly between registered memory regions on two machines, with no kernel copies and no remote CPU involvement. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Re-mirroring storm** — A cascade in which many volumes lose replicas at once and their simultaneous repair traffic exhausts capacity and network. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Read disturb** — Gradual shifting of unread NAND cells caused by the pass voltage applied during reads of other cells in the same block, forcing periodic data relocation. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Read retry** — Re-reading a NAND page at shifted reference voltages when error correction fails, at the cost of extra latency. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Read-after-write consistency** — A guarantee that once a write succeeds, every subsequent read returns the new data. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Read-modify-write penalty** — The extra NAND work when a write is smaller than the drive's indirection unit, forcing the whole unit to be read, merged and rewritten. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Real option** — A small, early investment that preserves the right to scale up if a trend breaks favorably. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Rebalancing** — Background movement of data to restore even placement after nodes are added or removed. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Rebuild storm** — The burst of east-west network and drive traffic generated while a cluster restores redundancy after a drive or node failure. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Rebuild window** — Time between a drive failure and restored full redundancy, during which further failures risk data loss. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Recall** — The share of the true nearest neighbours that an approximate search actually returns. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Recompute-versus-fetch break-even** — The per-GPU bandwidth above which loading stored KV is faster than recomputing it with prefill (roughly 2–5 GB/s for a 70B model). ([Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **Redirect-on-write (ROW) snapshot** — Snapshot method that freezes the pointer map and writes new data to free space. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Reducible data** — Data not already compressed or encrypted by the host, which is what most reduction guarantees cover. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Reference-design status** — Being named in a platform vendor's validated architecture, which works as a procurement shortlist for buyers. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Remaining performance obligations (RPO)** — contracted revenue not yet recognised, including undelivered product and subscription terms. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md), [Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Reported by press** — a label for a figure published by journalists, often from unnamed sources. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Reranker** — A second, more accurate model that rescores the top candidates from a vector search before they go into the prompt. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **Restore storm** — The burst of simultaneous reads and metadata operations when every GPU in a job loads the latest checkpoint after a failure. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Retimer** — An active chip that recovers and re-transmits a high-speed serial signal to extend link reach. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Revenue inflation** — revenue growth driven by higher selling prices rather than more units shipped. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Right-Size Guarantee** — Everpure's (originally Pure Storage's, 2016) workload-based guarantee of effective capacity for FlashArray purchases. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **RNIC** — A network interface card that implements the RDMA transport in hardware. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **RoCEv2** — RDMA over Converged Ethernet version 2: the InfiniBand transport carried in routable UDP/IP packets on Ethernet. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Rolling hash** — A hash recomputed cheaply as a window slides one byte at a time, used to find content-defined chunk boundaries (e.g., Rabin, Gear). ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Royalty / licence revenue** — Fees paid to an IP owner per unit deployed, with the customer buying the underlying hardware. ([Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **RPO (recovery point objective)** — The maximum amount of recent data, measured in time, an organisation can afford to lose. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **RPO (remaining performance obligations)** — Contracted revenue not yet recognized, disclosed under ASC 606. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **RTO (recovery time objective)** — The maximum time an organisation can afford a service to be down. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Rule of X** — Bessemer Venture Partners' growth-weighted variant of the Rule of 40: revenue growth times a multiplier (about 2–3) plus free-cash-flow margin. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))

## S

- **S3 (Simple Storage Service) API** — Amazon's HTTP/REST interface for object storage, now the de facto standard implemented by most storage vendors. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **S3 Express One Zone** — An AWS S3 storage class using single-Availability-Zone directory buckets for single-digit-millisecond access. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md), [Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **S3 over RDMA** — A data path in which a normal S3 request carries a memory token over HTTP while the object bytes move by RDMA directly to or from host or GPU memory. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md), [Ch 11](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/11-gpu-data-path.md))
- **S3 Tables** — AWS table buckets that store and automatically maintain Apache Iceberg tables inside S3. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **S3 Vectors** — An AWS S3 capability that stores and queries vector embeddings natively in vector buckets. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md), [Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **SafeMode** — Everpure's snapshot immutability feature, in which deleted snapshots are retained for a set period and cannot be eradicated without support-gated approval. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Sales engineer (SE)** — A pre-sales technical specialist who sizes systems, runs proofs of concept and answers technical objections in deals. ([Ch 57](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/57-question-bank.md))
- **SAM (serviceable addressable market)** — The part of a TAM a vendor can actually sell into given its products, channels and geographies. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **SAN (storage area network)** — A dedicated network giving many hosts block-level access to shared arrays. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md), [Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **SBOM (software bill of materials)** — A machine-readable list of the components and licences inside a piece of software. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD)** — AWS's multipath, reliable but out-of-order transport implemented in Nitro cards and used by EBS io2 Block Express. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Scalable unit (SU)** — The 32-node building block of a DGX SuperPOD (256 GPUs with eight-GPU nodes). ([Ch 34](docs/05-ai-storage/34-nvidia-ecosystem.md))
- **Scale-out** — Growing a storage system by adding whole nodes rather than upgrading a controller pair. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Scale-out NAS** — A file system spread across a cluster of nodes behind one namespace, grown by adding nodes rather than upgrading controllers. ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Scale-up** — Growing a storage system by adding drives or faster controllers behind a fixed controller pair rather than adding nodes. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Scrubbing** — A background process that re-reads stored data and verifies checksums to find and repair silent corruption (bit rot). ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **SCSI** — The Small Computer System Interface command set, standardized in 1986 and still carried over Fibre Channel and iSCSI. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Second-OS problem** — The engineering cost and customer confusion of running two storage operating systems after an acquisition. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Secondary storage** — The tier that holds backup, disaster-recovery and other copies of primary data, optimised for ingest, restore speed and cost. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Secondary tender** — A funding round in which investors buy existing shares from employees or early holders, so the company receives none of that money. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md), [Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **SEDA** — HPE's name for the shared-everything disaggregated architecture of its Alletra MP X10000. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Segment-fit heatmap** — A vendor-by-buyer-segment table showing where each vendor has proven, partial or little fit. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Sell-through** — The share of a neocloud's installed storage capacity actually billed to tenants, which drives its storage gross margin. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **Semantic layer** — A governed set of business definitions (metrics, dimensions, joins) that maps business terms such as "net revenue" onto underlying tables. ([Ch 39](docs/05-ai-storage/39-agentic-ai-and-data-intelligence.md))
- **SerDes** — Serializer/deserializer circuits whose per-lane rate (e.g., 112G, 224G) determines achievable port speeds. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Server attach** — Selling storage as an add-on to a server-led purchase, a key bundling tactic for server-and-storage vendors. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Server-based storage** — Drives inside general-purpose servers managed by software (HCI, SDS or a hyperscaler file system) rather than a dedicated array. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Shard** — A large file or object that packs many training samples together so storage serves big sequential reads instead of many small ones. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **ShardStore** — The key-value storage-node engine, written in Rust, that stores object shards on each Amazon S3 storage node. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Shared-nothing cluster** — A storage architecture in which each node owns its own CPUs, memory and drives, and nodes cooperate only by sending requests over the network. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Short-stroking** — Using only a hard drive's outer tracks to cut seek time, sacrificing most of its capacity for performance. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Signature visual** — a diagram marked ★ in the outline that a reader should be able to redraw from memory. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Signpost** — an observable, dated event that confirms or refutes a long-range technology thesis. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **SigV4** — AWS Signature Version 4, which signs each HTTP request with an HMAC-derived key so the server can authenticate it without the secret crossing the wire. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Similarity hash** — A fingerprint that gives close values for chunks sharing most of their bytes, unlike a cryptographic hash that changes completely with one byte. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Similarity reduction** — Storing near-identical blocks as compressed differences against a reference block found via a locality-sensitive hash. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Similarity-based data reduction** — A data-reduction method that groups nearly identical chunks and stores most of them as small deltas against a shared reference chunk. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Simulated accelerator** — a software stand-in for a GPU in MLPerf Storage that waits a calibrated time per batch instead of computing. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **Single namespace** — One file or object directory tree that all clients see, regardless of how many nodes store the data. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **Single-head bottleneck** — The limit reached when every byte of a NAS mount must pass through one server controller's CPU, memory and NICs. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **Single-mount ceiling** — The throughput one client mount can reach before extra connections or parallel paths are needed. ([Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **Site power cap** — The fixed grid allocation, in megawatts, that bounds all IT load a datacenter campus can run. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))
- **SLC / MLC / TLC / QLC / PLC** — NAND storing 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 bits per cell (2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 voltage states), trading endurance and speed for cost per bit. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **SLC cache** — Part of a TLC or QLC SSD run in 1-bit mode to absorb incoming writes quickly before they are folded into denser cells. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **SLED (single large expensive disk)** — The RAID paper's name for the big mainframe drives that arrays of small disks replaced. ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Small-file problem** — The collapse in effective throughput when files are so small that per-file metadata operations, not bandwidth, limit performance. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **Small-object tax** — The disproportionate request cost and rate-limit pressure incurred when data is stored as many small objects. ([Ch 9](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/09-object-storage-and-s3.md))
- **Smart client** — A client library that performs data placement, encoding and direct data transfer itself, removing the storage controller from the data path. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **SMB Direct** — SMB3 running over RDMA (iWARP, InfiniBand or RoCE) for low-latency, low-CPU file access. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **SMB Multichannel** — An SMB3 feature that automatically spreads one session over several network connections and adapters. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **SMB3** — The Windows file-sharing protocol version introduced with Windows Server 2012, adding Multichannel, SMB Direct and transparent failover. ([Ch 8](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/08-file-protocols.md))
- **SMR (shingled magnetic recording)** — HDD recording that overlaps tracks like roof shingles for more capacity, at the cost of having to rewrite whole bands or zones sequentially. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Software composition analysis** — Automated scanning of a code base to inventory its open-source components and their licences. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Software-defined storage** — Storage sold as software that runs on partner or customer servers rather than on the vendor's own appliances. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **Software-defined storage (SDS)** — Storage software sold separately from the hardware it runs on, deployed on commodity servers. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Software-defined wave** — A period when storage functions move from proprietary controllers onto commodity servers as software. ([Ch 51](docs/07-history-and-future/51-history-of-storage.md))
- **Software-only storage** — Storage software sold to run on customer- or partner-supplied commodity servers rather than as a vendor appliance. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **Solidigm** — The SK hynix subsidiary formed from Intel's NAND and SSD business in December 2021. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Sovereign AI** — AI infrastructure built so that data, control and operations stay within a given country or jurisdiction. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Sovereign cloud** — Cloud services run under local jurisdiction and control, often by domestic providers, to meet data-sovereignty rules. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Sovereign presence** — A vendor's ability to win deals that require in-country control of data and supply, typically government and national AI clouds. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Spaced repetition** — Reviewing material at increasing intervals, each timed to fall just before it would be forgotten. ([Ch 59](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/59-self-test-flashcards.md))
- **SPDK (Storage Performance Development Kit)** — A user-space library for driving NVMe devices directly with polling instead of kernel interrupts. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **SPECstorage Solution 2020** — SPEC's file-storage benchmark with five workloads (AI_IMAGE, EDA_BLENDED, GENOMICS, SWBUILD, VDA), each scored as a business metric at an overall response time. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **SPECstorage Solution 2020 AI_IMAGE** — a SPEC storage benchmark workload modelled on image-based AI training, scored in AI_Jobs at a response time. ([Ch 27](docs/04-everpure/27-flasharray-and-flashblade.md))
- **Spectrum-X** — NVIDIA's Ethernet platform pairing Spectrum switches with its NICs for adaptive routing and congestion control on AI fabrics. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Split-brain** — Failure state in which two partitioned copies both accept writes and diverge. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md), [Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **Spot price** — the price for memory traded in small, immediate lots outside long-term contracts, usually the first to move in a cycle. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **SSD controller** — The embedded system-on-chip inside an SSD, with processor cores, error-correction engines and flash channel interfaces, that runs the drive's firmware. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **STAC-M3** — an audited benchmark of kdb+ tick-data analytics used by financial-services buyers to compare storage and compute stacks. ([Ch 37](docs/05-ai-storage/37-reading-benchmarks.md))
- **Stateless controller** — A controller that holds no unique data or configuration, so it can be replaced without destaging or migrating anything. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Stock client** — the file-system client built into a standard operating system, such as the Linux NFS client, as opposed to a vendor's proprietary driver. ([Ch 0.2](docs/00-start-here/00b-one-page-map.md), [Ch 60](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/60-cheat-sheets.md))
- **Storage as code** — Declaring storage resources and policies in version-controlled automation (Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes manifests) instead of configuring them by hand. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Storage Availability Zone (SAZ)** — NetApp AFX's single shared pool of NVMe shelves that every controller can read and write. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Storage network** — The network, often converged with the front-end, that links GPU nodes to shared storage for training reads, checkpoints and KV-cache spill. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **Storage stack** — The ordered layers an I/O crosses from application to physical media: application, file system or object API, volume manager, protocol, network, array controller software, SSD controller/FTL and media. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
