- **Storage-as-a-service (STaaS)** — A model in which the vendor owns and operates storage at the customer's site and bills for consumption against service-level agreements. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **Storage-class memory (SCM)** — Persistent media faster than NAND but cheaper than DRAM, such as Intel Optane (3D XPoint). ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md), [Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Storage-only node** — An HCI node that contributes capacity but runs no application VMs, used to break coupled scaling. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **StorageClass** — A Kubernetes object naming a class of storage (performance, protection) that persistent volume claims request by name. ([Ch 22](docs/03-system-architecture/22-control-planes.md))
- **Stranded resources** — Compute or capacity that is bought only because a fixed node configuration bundles it with the resource actually needed. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Strategic fit** — Whether an option strengthens a layer customers pay for, or protects one they do pay for. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Strategic purchase** — buying components well ahead of need to secure supply and lock in cost, at the expense of near-term cash flow. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Stretched (metro) cluster** — Two arrays at nearby sites presenting the same volumes active/active over synchronous replication. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Stripe count** — The number of storage targets a file's chunks are dealt across, which sets its maximum parallel bandwidth. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Stripe size** — The size of each chunk a file is cut into before the chunks are spread across storage targets. ([Ch 17](docs/03-system-architecture/17-parallel-file-systems.md))
- **Stripe width** — The number of data plus parity strips in one erasure-coded stripe, e.g., 146+4; wider stripes mean lower capacity overhead. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **STX** — NVIDIA's BlueField-4 storage reference architecture, launched at GTC 2026, on which storage partners build AI storage nodes. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Submission queue / completion queue (SQ/CQ)** — NVMe's paired rings in host memory holding 64-byte commands and 16-byte completions. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **Subscription ARR** — The annualized run rate of recurring subscription revenue at period end. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md), [Ch 58](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/58-explain-in-30-seconds.md))
- **Substitution right** — A supplier's contractual right to swap the underlying asset; if substantive, it can mean a contract contains no lease. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md))
- **Subtree partitioning** — Scaling metadata by assigning whole directory subtrees to different metadata servers, statically or dynamically. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **SuperNIC** — NVIDIA's term for a high-bandwidth NIC tuned for AI east-west traffic, such as ConnectX-8/9. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **Symmetric active/active** — A controller arrangement in which every path is optimized and any controller can serve any volume. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **Synchronous checkpointing** — Pausing training until the checkpoint is fully written to durable storage. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))
- **Synchronous replication** — Replication that acknowledges a write only after both sites have persisted it, giving zero data loss. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **System-level TB/W** — Capacity per watt measured for a whole storage system including controllers, fans and networking, rather than for a bare drive. ([Ch 38](docs/05-ai-storage/38-power-and-density.md))

## T

- **Tail latency** — The latency of the slowest small fraction of requests, expressed as a high percentile such as p99 or p99.9. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Take-or-pay contract** — A multi-year commitment in which a customer pays for reserved GPU capacity whether or not it uses it, used by neoclouds to secure financing. ([Ch 35](docs/05-ai-storage/35-ai-factories-and-neoclouds.md))
- **Takeover / giveback** — A partner controller assuming a failed or upgrading controller's volumes, then returning them when it rejoins. ([Ch 14](docs/03-system-architecture/14-scale-up-dual-controller.md))
- **TAM (total addressable market)** — The total annual spend a product category could capture if it won every deal in its defined scope. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Target** — The device or array side of a block-storage session that executes commands from initiators. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
- **TB/RU** — Storage capacity per rack unit (1.75 inches of rack height), a density metric. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **TB/W** — Storage capacity per watt of power drawn, a key efficiency metric for power-constrained data centres. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **TCV (total contract value)** — The full value of a contract signed in a period, regardless of when revenue is recognized. ([Ch 23](docs/03-system-architecture/23-consumption-models.md), [Ch 29](docs/04-everpure/29-hyperscaler-ecosystem-financials.md))
- **Technical due diligence** — Verification of a target's technology claims, risks and integration cost before a deal is signed. ([Ch 50](docs/06-industry-and-competition/50-diligence-framework.md))
- **Technical fit** — Whether an acquired or partnered asset can run on, or beside, the existing operating system and control plane without adding a second data path. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **Technology licensing model** — A commercial structure in which the customer sources its own hardware and NAND and pays the supplier for software, IP and support. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md))
- **Technology radar** — A chart placing trends by maturity ring and category to show what to adopt now and what to watch. ([Ch 53](docs/07-history-and-future/53-future-trends.md))
- **Tectonic** — Meta's exabyte-scale multitenant distributed file system, one cluster per datacenter. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Term (Raft)** — Raft's logical clock; each term has at most one leader, and a node seeing a higher term steps down. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Tested limit** — the largest configuration a vendor has validated and supports, as opposed to its architectural maximum. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Thin provisioning** — Allocating physical capacity to a volume only when data is actually written, rather than at creation. ([Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Throughput** — Data moved per second (e.g., GB/s), equal to IOPS multiplied by I/O size; usually quoted for large sequential transfers. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Throughput-bound workload** — A workload whose performance depends on aggregate bytes per second across many parallel streams, such as AI training data loading. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **TiB (tebibyte)** — 2^40 bytes, about 9% smaller than a decimal terabyte (10^12 bytes). ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Tier 0** — Hammerspace's shared, protected storage tier built from the local NVMe drives inside GPU servers. ([Ch 47](docs/06-industry-and-competition/47-other-challengers.md))
- **Tiering (lifecycle management)** — Policy-driven movement of data between storage tiers as its access pattern or value changes. ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Time to first token (TTFT)** — The latency from submitting a prompt to receiving the first generated token, the key inference responsiveness metric. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md), [Ch 32](docs/05-ai-storage/32-inference-and-kv-cache.md))
- **Tintri** — A virtualisation-focused storage vendor whose assets DDN bought out of bankruptcy in 2018 and still sells as Tintri VMstore. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **Token** — The unit of text (roughly a word fragment) that a language model reads and predicts; dataset sizes are usually quoted in tokens. ([Ch 30](docs/05-ai-storage/30-ai-data-pipeline.md))
- **Token warehouse** — WEKA's marketing term for the pooled NVMe store that holds KV-cache blocks for reuse across GPU servers. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Total cost of ownership (TCO)** — All costs of a system over a stated period: acquisition, power, space, support, refresh and operations. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Total efficiency** — A vendor ratio that adds thin-provisioning and snapshot savings on top of data reduction, and is therefore larger and softer than DRR. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md), [Ch 5](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/05-data-reduction.md))
- **Total enterprise storage systems** — External arrays plus server-based storage and ODM-direct hyperscaler purchases; IDC no longer publicises this total. ([Ch 40](docs/06-industry-and-competition/40-market-structure.md))
- **Tracker estimate** — a market figure from an analyst tracker such as IDC's, valid only on that tracker's definitions. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **TrafficGroup** — A Tectonic grouping of tenants that share resource quotas such as IOPS. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **TRIM / Deallocate** — A host command telling the drive that logical blocks no longer hold useful data, so garbage collection can skip them. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **Tuck-in acquisition** — A small acquisition that buys a capability or team to fold into an existing product rather than buying a large revenue base. ([Ch 25](docs/04-everpure/25-company-history-and-strategy.md), [Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))

## U

- **Ultra Ethernet (UEC / UET)** — An industry consortium and its 2025 specification for an Ethernet-based AI/HPC transport that tolerates lossy fabrics. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **UltraSMR** — Western Digital's shingled magnetic recording technology, which overlaps tracks to raise HDD capacity at the cost of slower random writes. ([Ch 48](docs/06-industry-and-competition/48-media-suppliers-and-nand-cycle.md))
- **Unified Cache Manager (UCM)** — Huawei's KV-cache tiering software that moves inference context across memory and storage tiers to reduce HBM needs. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))
- **Unified storage** — A single storage system that serves more than one abstraction (block, file and/or object). ([Ch 1](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/01-what-storage-does.md))
- **Unified storage platform** — A system or product family that serves block, file and object from one software stack or control plane. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **Unrecoverable read error (URE)** — A sector the drive cannot read back even after retries, specified as a rate per bits read. ([Ch 6](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/06-data-protection-and-resilience.md))
- **Usable capacity** — Capacity left after parity, rebuild spares, metadata and system reserves are deducted from raw. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))
- **Utilization** — The fraction of time a resource (die, CPU, port, disk arm) is busy; latency rises sharply as it approaches 100%. ([Ch 4](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/04-performance-and-economics-metrics.md))

## V

- **V-NAND** — Samsung's name for its 3D NAND, first mass-produced at 24 layers in 2013. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Value stack** — The layers of an industry ranked by where profit is captured, rather than by the technical path an I/O takes. ([Ch 54](docs/07-history-and-future/54-strategic-option-map.md))
- **VAST AgentEngine** — VAST's runtime for deploying AI agents with MCP-compatible tool access, announced in May 2025. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **VAST AI Operating System (AI OS)** — VAST's May 2025 umbrella brand for its storage services (DataStore, DataBase, DataSpace) plus compute engines such as DataEngine, InsightEngine and AgentEngine. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **VAST Amplify** — VAST's January 2026 programme to assess and reuse customers' installed NVMe SSDs, including competitors', during the NAND shortage. ([Ch 41](docs/06-industry-and-competition/41-why-ai-native-vendors-won.md))
- **VAST DataBase** — A columnar table store built directly into VAST's Element Store and queried through engines such as Trino and Spark. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **VAST DataEngine** — VAST's in-cluster event-trigger and serverless-function layer that runs code when data arrives or changes. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **VAST DataSpace** — VAST's global namespace that spans clusters, sites and clouds. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **VAST InsightEngine** — VAST's service that embeds and indexes new data as it lands (using NVIDIA NIM) for retrieval-augmented generation. ([Ch 42](docs/06-industry-and-competition/42-vast-data.md))
- **Vector database** — Software that stores embeddings and answers nearest-neighbour similarity queries, usually with metadata filters. ([Ch 33](docs/05-ai-storage/33-rag-vector-lakehouse.md))
- **VERIFY tag** — an inline marker for a claim not yet confirmed by a primary or second source, collected in the open-questions list. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Vertical integration (storage)** — Owning several adjacent stack layers, for example array software, flash translation and module design, as one engineered product. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **Vertically integrated storage** — A storage system whose vendor designs and supplies both the software and key hardware, such as controllers and flash modules. ([Ch 49](docs/06-industry-and-competition/49-competitive-matrices.md))
- **Virtual metadata server** — A software metadata owner running inside WEKA's compute processes on every node, replacing a dedicated metadata server. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Virtual nodes** — Many points on a consistent-hashing ring assigned to each physical server to even out load. ([Ch 15](docs/03-system-architecture/15-scale-out-shared-nothing.md))
- **VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF)** — Broadcom's main VMware subscription bundle, licensed per core, combining vSphere, vSAN, NSX and management tools. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **Volume manager** — Host or hypervisor software that pools and remaps block addresses across devices, such as LVM or software RAID. ([Ch 13](docs/03-system-architecture/13-storage-stack.md))
- **vSAN** — VMware's HCI storage software, which runs inside the ESXi hypervisor kernel and pools node-local drives. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **vSAN Max** — A VMware deployment model that builds a storage-only vSAN cluster mounted by separate compute clusters. ([Ch 19](docs/03-system-architecture/19-software-defined-and-hci.md))
- **VSP One** — Hitachi Vantara's storage brand covering block, file and object systems. ([Ch 46](docs/06-industry-and-competition/46-incumbents.md))

## W

- **Wafer bonding (NAND)** — Building the NAND's CMOS control logic on a separate wafer and bonding it to the memory array wafer. ([Ch 2](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/02-media-physics.md))
- **Wafer spot price** — The open-market price for unpackaged NAND wafers, quoted per die-equivalent (e.g., per 512Gb unit), a fast-moving indicator of NAND pricing. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Wafer starts** — The number of wafers a fab begins processing per month, the physical measure of memory capacity. ([Ch 52](docs/07-history-and-future/52-history-of-flash.md))
- **Wear levelling** — FTL logic that spreads program/erase cycles evenly across blocks so no part of the flash wears out early. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md))
- **WebDataset** — A data-loading format and library that packs training samples into large tar shards so they can be read sequentially. ([Ch 21](docs/03-system-architecture/21-metadata.md))
- **WekaFS** — WEKA's original parallel, POSIX-compliant file system for NVMe flash with tiering to object storage. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **WEKApod** — WEKA's branded storage appliance line; WEKApod 3 (2026) offers Nitro, Prime and Prime Max configurations. ([Ch 43](docs/06-industry-and-competition/43-weka.md))
- **Whamcloud** — The Lustre engineering company bought by Intel in 2012 and revived as a DDN division after DDN bought Intel's Lustre business in 2018. ([Ch 44](docs/06-industry-and-competition/44-ddn.md))
- **Whiteboard prompt** — a request to sketch a mechanism, such as a write path, to test L2 understanding. ([Ch 56](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/56-talking-with-engineering-and-cto.md))
- **Win/loss review** — a structured analysis of why specific deals were won or lost, and on which attribute. ([Ch 55](docs/08-conversation-toolkit/55-talking-with-pms.md))
- **Witness** — A data-less third voter, placed outside both sites' failure domains, that breaks ties in a two-site cluster. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Worked example** — arithmetic on stated assumptions, shown on the page so it can be checked. ([Ch 0.1](docs/00-start-here/00a-how-to-use-this-atlas.md))
- **Workload fit** — How naturally an architecture's design matches a workload's access pattern, protocol, latency and scale needs. ([Ch 24](docs/03-system-architecture/24-architecture-decision-matrix.md))
- **Write amplification factor (WAF)** — The ratio of bytes written to NAND to bytes written by the host, driven mainly by garbage collection. ([Ch 3](docs/01-storage-fundamentals/03-inside-an-ssd.md), [Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Write buffer** — A small persistent tier that absorbs and acknowledges writes before they are reorganized and written to capacity media. ([Ch 16](docs/03-system-architecture/16-disaggregated-shared-everything.md))
- **Write quorum** — The minimum number of fragment or replica writes that must succeed before a write is treated as durable. ([Ch 18](docs/03-system-architecture/18-object-storage-architecture.md))
- **Write-back cache** — A cache that acknowledges writes before the slower tier persists them, safe only if the cache is persistent and mirrored. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))
- **Write-through cache** — A cache that acknowledges writes only after the slower tier has persisted them. ([Ch 20](docs/03-system-architecture/20-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md))

## Y

- **Young's formula** — The classic approximation for the optimal checkpoint interval, the square root of two times the checkpoint cost times the mean time between failures. ([Ch 31](docs/05-ai-storage/31-training-storage.md))

## Z

- **Zero-copy** — Transferring data between memory and the wire without the CPU copying it between buffers. ([Ch 10](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/10-datacenter-networking.md))
- **ZippyDB** — Meta's sharded, replicated key-value store, used by Tectonic to hold its layered metadata. ([Ch 36](docs/05-ai-storage/36-hyperscaler-ai-storage.md))
- **Zoned Namespaces (ZNS)** — An NVMe command set that exposes zones which must be written sequentially and reset by the host. ([Ch 12](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/12-interfaces-and-emerging-tech.md))
- **Zoning** — A Fibre Channel switch-level access-control list defining which hosts can see which storage ports. ([Ch 7](docs/02-protocols-and-networking/07-block-protocols.md))
